<h1 id="here-tracking">HERE Tracking v2.1.191</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

HERE Tracking is a cloud product designed to address location tracking problems for a wide range of Location IoT industry verticals.

HERE Tracking also includes end-user mobile and web applications that can be used to demonstrate the product.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://tracking.api.here.com/">https://tracking.api.here.com/</a>

License: <a href="https://legal.here.com/en-gb/terms/documentation-license">HERE Documentation License</a>

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer A token obtained from a separate endpoint using client credentials and an OAuth 1.0a HMAC-SHA256 signed request.

Users are authenticated using an OAuth 1.0 bearer token obtained using the `/users/v2/login` endpoint.

Devices are authenticated using an OAuth 1.0 bearer token obtained using the `/v2/token` endpoint.

Make a request using the bearer token for authentication
---

Make a request with an `Authorization` header containing the obtained bearer token.

Example:

```
    Authorization: Bearer h1.yxPIksZ0ViLq77f1Nh-9cg.NVgGBZVlCU8G7kjV_...
```

> **Note:** For the available authentication options, see the [Identity & Access Management Guide](https://developer.here.com/documentation/identity-access-management/dev_guide/index.html).

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: oauth HERE Tracking requires that you sign your requests for tokens. The signature method uses the OAuth 1.0 standard. For more information on this standard, see the [OAuth Core 1.0](https://oauth.net/core/1.0/) specification.

> **Note:** You must create a new signature for each token request to HERE Tracking. Signatures can only be used once.

Create the Signature Base String
---

The first step in creating a signature is to create the signature base string. This string contains the parameters to use when generating the signature.

*1. To begin, make sure you have the information listed in the following table.*

| Parameter                | Description                              |
| ------------------------ | -----------------------------------------|
| oauth\_consumer\_key     | The device ID for which you want to generate a token. |
| oauth\_signature\_method | Always use "HMAC-SHA256".                 |
| oauth\_timestamp         | The number of seconds since the Unix epoch at the point the request is generated. This must be within 10 seconds of the timestamp returned by the `/v2/timestamp` endpoint. |
| oauth\_nonce             | A unique string for this signature. The string cannot have been used in a previous signature. Each token generation request to HERE Tracking must have a unique signature, and the value in this parameter is what is used to ensure the signature is unique. |
| oauth\_version           | Always use "1.0".                         |

*2. Combine these values into a single string by following these steps:*

   1. URL encode every key and value.
   2. Sort the list of key-value pairs alphabetically by key.
   3. Concatenate each key/value pair, separating each with an ampersand character ("&").

The result is a parameter string that looks like this (line breaks are added for legibility):

   ```
   oauth_consumer_key=47164fb0-b7b3-49e8-891b-650270b82cf2
   &oauth_nonce=LIIpk4
   &oauth_signature_method=HMAC-SHA256
   &oauth_timestamp=1513634609
   &oauth_version=1.0
   ```

*3. Combine the HTTP method, base URL, and parameter string into a single string called the "base string". This will be the string from which the signature is generated. The base string is in this format:*

   ```
   POST&https://tracking.api.here.com/v2/token&<URL encoded parameter string>
   ```

   The base string consists of:

   1. The HTTP method in caps (POST) followed by an ampersand ("&")
   2. The URL of the HERE Tracking token endpoint followed by an ampersand ("&")
   3. The URL-encoded parameter string.

   For example (line breaks are added for legibility):

   ```
   POST
    &https%3A%2F%2Ftracking.api.here.com%2Fv2%2Ftoken
    &oauth_consumer_key%3D47164fb0-b7b3-49e8-891b-650270b82cf2%26
    oauth_nonce%3DLIIpk4%26oauth_signature_method%3DHMAC-SHA256%26
    oauth_timestamp%3D1513634609%26oauth_version%3D1.0
   ```

   > **Note:** The URL-encoded base string should contain exactly two ampersands ("&").

Create the signature
---

The signing key used to sign the base string is the `deviceSecret` followed by an ampersand ("&").

Create the signature by passing the signature base string and the signing key to the `HMAC-SHA256` hashing algorithm and converting the result to a `base64` string. Then, use the signature to request a token.

Request the token
---

Make a `POST` request to this endpoint with an `Authorization` header constructed from the above parameters and the generated signature.

Example:

```
    Authorization: OAuth oauth_consumer_key="47164fb0-b7b3-49e8-891b-650270b82cf2",
        oauth_signature_method="HMAC-SHA256",
        oauth_timestamp="1513634609",
        oauth_nonce="LIIpk4",
        oauth_version="1.0",
        oauth_signature="pQ9EJX14L736B%2Br7uZl4yQlO6Xw%3D"
```

<h1 id="here-tracking-ingestion">Ingestion</h1>

The ingestion service provides an interface for devices to do data ingestion to HERE Tracking.
The ingested data is a device telemetry, which may include, for example, a GPS position, sensor readings,
WLAN or Bluetooth scans.
Only a provisioned and a claimed device data is accepted.

Devices should use uniquely this interface to send data to HERE Tracking.


## Ingests data and receives a shadow

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "scan": {
        "gsm": [
          {
            "cid": 16504,
            "lac": 5126,
            "mcc": 262,
            "mnc": 1,
            "nmr": [
              {
                "bcch": "82",
                "bsic": "6"
              },
              {
                "bcch": "85",
                "bsic": "7"
              },
              {
                "bcch": "93",
                "bsic": "12"
              },
              {
                "bcch": "88",
                "bsic": "13"
              },
              {
                "bcch": "88",
                "bsic": "19"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      },
      "timestamp": 1515169948976
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /v2/`

Devices can use this end point to ingest data into HERE Tracking,
in the same way as via the `/v3` endpoint.

A device uses its access token obtained via the the `/v2/token` endpoint
to send telemetry – GPS position, sensor readings, WLAN or Bluetooth scans - to HERE Tracking.

By default the request is synchronous and the response will be
the device `desired` shadow. If the request is set
to be asynchronous, the response will be empty.

The device position gets resolved based on the `position` and `scan` objects
provided in the request body (see the objects definitions for details).
If only `position` is provided, it will be used as the device position.
If only `scan` is provided, the position will be resolved asynchronously
via the HERE Positioning API after returning a response.
If both are provided, `scan` is resolved to a position via the HERE Positioning API,
and the better of the two positions (provided vs. resolved) will be selected.
If neither `position` nor `scan` is provided, or if the HERE Positioning API is not able to
resolve the position, the device position will be left empty.

The `reported` shadow will be updated with the device latest position information,
sensor readings and settings ingested by the device.
The reported shadow may also contain additional properties generated by HERE
Tracking based on the device-ingested telemetry.
Such properties are stored in the `system.computed` property of the shadow.
The device shadow can be queried via the `shadows/v2/{trackingId}` endpoint.

The data ingested by the device will be available as a device trace via the `traces/v2/{trackingId}` endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "scan": {
      "gsm": [
        {
          "cid": 16504,
          "lac": 5126,
          "mcc": 262,
          "mnc": 1,
          "nmr": [
            {
              "bcch": "82",
              "bsic": "6"
            },
            {
              "bcch": "85",
              "bsic": "7"
            },
            {
              "bcch": "93",
              "bsic": "12"
            },
            {
              "bcch": "88",
              "bsic": "13"
            },
            {
              "bcch": "88",
              "bsic": "19"
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "timestamp": 1515169948976
  }
]
```

<h3 id="ingests-data-and-receives-a-shadow-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful<br><br>The device data was ingested and processed successfully and the `desired` shadow<br>was returned.<br><br>This response is returned if the `async` query parameter was not set to `true`.<br>|Inline|
|204|No Content|Successful (no content).<br><br>The device data was ingested successfully and the response is empty.<br>This response is returned if the `async` query parameter was set to `true`.<br>|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request<br><br>The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range.<br><br>If available, further error details are provided in the response body.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized<br><br>The request did not provide correct authentication details<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden<br><br>The account does not have the correct privileges<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found<br><br>The specified resource was not found<br>|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload Too Large<br><br>The request size exceeds the maximum size limit for payloads.<br>|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate limited.<br><br>When a device exceeds the number of requests allowed in plan configured for the `appId`, it will receive "Too Many Requests" 429 error code along with following headers:<br><br>\| header                    \| description                               \|<br>\| ------------------------  \| ----------------------------------------- \|<br>\| X-RateLimit-Remaining     \| The remaining number of requests          \|<br>\| X-RateLimit-Limit         \| The allowed number of requests for the `appId` plan \|<br>\| Retry-After               \| The number of seconds the device needs to wait before retrying the data ingestion \|<br>|Inline|

|» detectOutliers|boolean|false|none|A boolean value that sets outlier detection on or off|
|» disableTracking|object|false|none|Tracking can be disabled and enabled by defining disableTracking object.<br>In order to disable tracking, one must at least provide the begin time of the disabling<br>period and define either position or sensor properties one wants to disable. One can also<br>disable both position and sensors at the same time. By default tracking is enabled.<br>|
|» » periods|[object]|false|none|Define begin and end of the disabling period. All trace points with timestamp that falls between begin and end times will be disabled according to the settings defined in the position and sensors properties.<br>|
|» » » begin|integer|false|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC<br><br>Begin time of the tracking disabling period.<br><br>Begin must be smaller than end. Begin must be greater or equal to current time.<br>Begin can be set without end. If there exists already end time which is earlier<br>than given new begin time, the existing end time will be deleted.<br>|
|» » » end|integer|false|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC<br><br>End time of the tracking disabling period.<br><br>End must be greater than begin. End must be greater or equal to current time.<br>End can be set without begin if begin is already set.<br>|
|» » position|string \| [string]|false|none|Define position methods to be disabled|

## Gets the current timestamp

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/timestamp \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /v2/timestamp`

Returns the current server time in seconds since the UNIX epoch.
The server time is used to check the validity of the OAuth 1.0 header of a device data ingestion request.
Devices must synchronise with the server time to avoid a clock skew.

> Note that in the data ingestion request the timestamp is specified in milliseconds.


<h3 id="gets-the-current-timestamp-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "timestamp": 2
}
```

```json
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

```json
  },
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The provided credentials are not valid."
}
```

## Requests a token for a registered device

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /v2/token`

Authenticates a device to HERE Tracking and requests a device access token.

A device must provide a valid device access token when it sends telemetry to HERE Tracking.
Tokens can be obtained upon a successful device authentication.

The device token requests must be signed. The signature method uses the OAuth 1.0 standard.
For more information on this standard, see the [OAuth Core 1.0](https://oauth.net/core/1.0/) specification.

Tokens can be requested only by claimed devices.
A claimed device license, that is ```deviceId``` and ```deviceSecret``` credential pair, is used for creating a signed token request.

> See the Authentication section for details on how to generate a signed token request.
> A new signature must be created for each device access token request.
> Signatures can only be used once.


<h3 id="requests-a-token-for-a-registered-device-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|authorization|header|string|true|Signed OAuth 1.0 header|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Ingests data for a device and receives a shadow

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v3/ \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "appId": "MyAppId123",
    "data": [
      {
        "scan": {
          "gsm": [
            {
              "cid": 16504,
              "lac": 5126,
              "mcc": 262,
              "mnc": 1,
              "nmr": [
                {
                  "bcch": "82",
                  "bsic": "6"
                },
                {
                  "bcch": "85",
                  "bsic": "7"
                },
                {
                  "bcch": "93",
                  "bsic": "12"
                },
                {
                  "bcch": "88",
                  "bsic": "13"
                },
                {
                  "bcch": "88",
                  "bsic": "19"
                }
              ]
            }
          ]
        },
        "timestamp": 1515169948976
      }
    ],
    "id": "MyDevice1"
  }'
```

`POST /v3/`

Devices can use this end point to ingest data into HERE Tracking.

A device uses its access token obtained via the the `/v2/token` endpoint
to send telemetry – GPS position, sensor readings, WLAN or Bluetooth scans - to HERE Tracking.

Also device owners use this end point to ingest data on behalf of a device.

The device can be either a real or a virtual device.
A real device is identified by a `trackingId` assigned to it when the device was claimed.
A virtual device is identified by an external device ID and the owner's project `appId`.

In case the ingestion is done by a device owner, the owner should first authenticate himself with
HERE Tracking and obtain a user access token via the `/users/v2/login` endpoint.
The user access token will then be used in this API call.

By default the request is synchronous and the response will be
the device `desired` shadow. If the request is set
to be asynchronous, the response will be empty.

The device position gets resolved based on the `position` and `scan` objects
provided in the request body (see the objects definitions for details).
If only `position` is provided, it will be used as the device position.
If only `scan` is provided, the position will be resolved asynchronously
via the HERE Positioning API after returning a response.
If both are provided, `scan` is resolved to a position via the HERE Positioning API,
and the better of the two positions (provided vs. resolved) will be selected.
If neither `position` nor `scan` is provided, or if the HERE Positioning API is not able to
resolve the position, the device position will be left empty.

The `reported` shadow will be updated with the device latest position information,
sensor readings and settings ingested by the device.
The reported shadow may also contain additional properties generated by HERE
Tracking based on the device-ingested telemetry.
Such properties are stored in the `system.computed` property of the shadow.
The device shadow can be queried via the `shadows/v2/{trackingId}` endpoint.

The data ingested by the device will be available as a device trace via the `traces/v2/{trackingId}` endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "appId": "MyAppId123",
  "data": [
    {
      "scan": {
        "gsm": [
          {
            "cid": 16504,
            "lac": 5126,
            "mcc": 262,
            "mnc": 1,
            "nmr": [
              {
                "bcch": "82",
                "bsic": "6"
              },
              {
                "bcch": "85",
                "bsic": "7"
              },
              {
                "bcch": "93",
                "bsic": "12"
              },
              {
                "bcch": "88",
                "bsic": "13"
              },
              {
                "bcch": "88",
                "bsic": "19"
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      },
      "timestamp": 1515169948976
    }
  ],
  "id": "MyDevice1"
}
```

|body|body|object|false|A device telemetry data.<br><br>The timestamp specifies the time in milliseconds at which the device telemetry measurements were taken.<br>This must be within 10 seconds of the timestamp returned by the `/v2/timestamp` endpoint.<br><br>Example of a GSM telemetry<br>---<br><br>```<br>[{<br>    "scan": {<br>        "gsm": [{<br>            "mcc": 262,<br>            "mnc": 1,<br>            "lac": 5126,<br>            "cid": 16504,<br>            "nmr": [<br>                { "bsic": "6", "bcch": "82" },<br>                { "bsic": "7", "bcch": "85" },<br>                { "bsic": "12", "bcch": "93" },<br>                { "bsic": "13", "bcch": "88" },<br>                { "bsic": "19", "bcch": "88" }<br>            ]<br>        }]<br>    },<br>    "payload": {<br>        "sensor": "data"<br>    },<br>    "timestamp": 1515169948976<br>}]<br>```<br><br>Example of a WLAN telemetry<br>---<br><br>```<br>[{<br>    "scan": {<br>        "wlan": [<br>            { "mac": "1c:1d:86:07:01:0f", "powrx": -45 },<br>            { "mac": "e4:f4:c6:d9:85:59", "powrx": -39 },<br>            { "mac": "1c:1d:86:07:01:0d", "powrx": -43 },<br>            { "mac": "1c:1d:86:07:01:0b", "powrx": -44 },<br>            { "mac": "1c:1d:86:07:01:04", "powrx": -58 },<br>            { "mac": "1c:1d:86:07:01:03", "powrx": -59 }<br>        ]<br>    },<br>    "payload": {<br>        "sensor": "data"<br>    },<br>    "timestamp": 1515169948976<br>}]<br>```<br>|

<h3 id="ingests-data-for-a-device-and-receives-a-shadow-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful<br><br>The device data was ingested and processed successfully and the `desired` shadow<br>was returned.<br><br>This response is returned if the `async` query parameter was not set to `true`.<br>|Inline|
|204|No Content|Successful (no content).<br><br>The device data was ingested successfully and the response is empty.<br>This response is returned if the `async` query parameter was set to `true`.<br>|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request<br><br>The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range.<br><br>If available, further error details are provided in the response body.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized<br><br>The request did not provide correct authentication details<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden<br><br>The account does not have the correct privileges<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found<br><br>The specified resource was not found<br>|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Payload Too Large<br><br>The request size exceeds the maximum size limit for payloads.<br>|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Rate limited.<br><br>When a device exceeds the number of requests allowed in plan configured for the `appId`, it will receive "Too Many Requests" 429 error code along with following headers:<br><br>\| header                    \| description                               \|<br>\| ------------------------  \| ----------------------------------------- \|<br>\| X-RateLimit-Remaining     \| The remaining number of requests          \|<br>\| X-RateLimit-Limit         \| The allowed number of requests for the `appId` plan \|<br>\| Retry-After               \| The number of seconds the device needs to wait before retrying the data ingestion \|<br>|Inline|

<h3 id="ingests-data-for-a-device-and-receives-a-shadow-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|payload|object|false|none|A free format JSON object.<br>The maximum size is 1000B.<br>|
|system|object|false|none|Contains device configuration settings.<br>|
|» detectOutliers|boolean|false|none|A boolean value that sets outlier detection on or off|
|» disableTracking|object|false|none|Tracking can be disabled and enabled by defining disableTracking object.<br>In order to disable tracking, one must at least provide the begin time of the disabling<br>period and define either position or sensor properties one wants to disable. One can also<br>disable both position and sensors at the same time. By default tracking is enabled.<br>|
|» » periods|[object]|false|none|Define begin and end of the disabling period. All trace points with timestamp that falls between begin and end times will be disabled according to the settings defined in the position and sensors properties.<br>|
|» » » begin|integer|false|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC<br><br>Begin time of the tracking disabling period.<br><br>Begin must be smaller than end. Begin must be greater or equal to current time.<br>Begin can be set without end. If there exists already end time which is earlier<br>than given new begin time, the existing end time will be deleted.<br>|
|» » » end|integer|false|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC<br><br>End time of the tracking disabling period.<br><br>End must be greater than begin. End must be greater or equal to current time.<br>End can be set without begin if begin is already set.<br>|
|» » position|string \| [string]|false|none|Define position methods to be disabled|
|» » » *oneOf*|string|false|none|All positioning data the device sends will be removed before further processing. No geofence and location events will be generated<br>|
|» » » *oneOf*|[string]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[string]|false|none|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|string|false|none|By setting the position property empty string, all positioning data will be re-enabled during the disabling period.<br>|
|» » sensors|string \| [string]|false|none|Define sensors to be disabled|
|» » » *oneOf*|string|false|none|All sensor data the device sends will be removed before further processing. No sensor events will be generated.<br>|
|» » » *oneOf*|[string]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[string]|false|none|none|
|» » » *oneOf*|string|false|none|By setting the sensors property empty string, all sensors data will be re-enabled during the disabling period.<br>|
|» lastModifiedGeofenceTimestamp|integer|true|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The time of the last update to geofences that device is associated<br>with. This value is zero when device hasn't yet been associated with<br>any geofence. This is set by HERE Tracking when any geofences<br>associated with the device is modified or removed. Also adding and<br>removing geofence associations update this value.<br>|
|» rate|object|false|none|This can be used to specify the rates at which the device performs certain tasks.|
|» » distanceM|number|false|none|Send an update if the device has moved farther than the specified distance in meters|
|» » sampleMs|number|false|none|The rate at which to sample signals in milliseconds|
|» » sendMs|number|false|none|The rate at which to send sample results in milliseconds|
|» sensorAlarmConfig|object|false|none|The device sensors alarm configuration.<br>|
|» » alertAccelerationGMax|number|false|none|An upper threshold value for acceleration in g-forces.|
|» » alertAccelerationGMin|number|false|none|A lower threshold value for acceleration in g-forces.|
|» » alertBatteryLevelPMax|number|false|none|An upper threshold value for battery level percentage.|
|» » alertBatteryLevelPMin|number|false|none|A lower threshold value for battery level percentage.|
|» » alertPressureHpaMax|number|false|none|An upper threshold value for pressure in hectopascals.|
|» » alertPressureHpaMin|number|false|none|A lower threshold value for pressure in hectopascals.|
|» » alertRelativeHumidityMax|number|false|none|An upper threshold value for relative humidity percentage.|
|» » alertRelativeHumidityMin|number|false|none|A lower threshold value for relative humidity percentage.|
|» » alertTemperatureCMax|number|false|none|An upper threshold value for temperature in degrees Celsius.|
|» » alertTemperatureCMin|number|false|none|A lower threshold value for temperature in degrees Celsius.|
|» » alertTiltDegreeMax|number|false|none|An upper threshold value for tilt in degrees.|
|» » alertTiltDegreeMin|number|false|none|A lower threshold value for tilt in degrees.|
|» » isAttachAlertEnabled|boolean|false|none|True if attach sensor alert in device is enabled.|
|» » isTamperAlertEnabled|boolean|false|none|True if tamper sensor alert in device is enabled.|
|» sensorLoggingConfigurations|[object]|false|none|An array of objects that holds sensor logging configurations|
|» » samplingFrequency|number|false|none|Sampling frequrency of single sensor loggin configuration (in milliseconds)|
|» » type|string|true|none|Type of single sensor logging configuration|
|» sensorLoggingEnabled|boolean|false|none|Flag that sets sensor logging on or off|
|» stateVersion|integer|true|none|The version of the state of a device. This should be incremented only by HERE Tracking.<br>|
|» syncGeofences|boolean|false|none|A boolean value that sets efficient geofencing on or off|
|» wlanConfigurations|[object]|false|none|An array of objects that holds wlan configurations|
|» » password|string|false|none|WLAN password. Please note that the password is stored to the device unencrypted. Do not use secure private networks, such as Intranet, for tracker WLAN connectivity. Password is required if security mode is other then 'none'.|
|» » securityMode|string|true|none|Selected security mode|
|» » ssid|string|true|none|Name given to a WLAN that is used by the client to access a WLAN network. Please note that the SSID is stored to the device unencrypted. Do not use secure private networks, such as Intranet, for tracker WLAN connectivity.|
|» » ssidIsHidden|boolean|false|none|Flag that informs if SSID is hidden|
|» wlanConnectivityEnabled|boolean|false|none|A boolean value that sets wlan connectivity on or off|
|timestamp|integer|false|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The time of the last update to the desired shadow.<br>|

```bash
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "appId": "MyAppId123",
    "data": [

  }'
```

`POST /v3/batch`

Device owner use this endpoint to ingest data to HERE Tracking on behalf of multiple devices.

A single request can contain data for multiple devices.
The devices can be either real or virtual.
A real device is identified by a `trackingId` assigned to it when the device was claimed.
A virtual device is identified by an external device ID and the owner's project `appId`.

Prior to making the request, the device owner should first authenticate himself with
HERE Tracking and obtain a user access token.
The user access token will then be used in this API call.

For more information on the device position resolution, and the device shadow and trace updates,
see the `/v3` endpoint description.

<h3 id="ingests-data-for-multiple-devices-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

<h1 id="here-tracking-largedata">Largedata</h1>

The Largedata service is used for storing large data blobs from devices to
HERE Tracking and retrieving the resulting assembled data from HERE Tracking by the users.

The data upload from a device follows the multipart data upload pattern:

* Create a new data upload.
* Check that the upload status is no longer ***preparing***.
* For each part:
** Upload the part.
* Complete the upload after all parts have been uploaded.

A data upload state can be one of the following:
* ***preparing***: The storage for the data is being prepared.
* ***pending***: Data upload has been succesfully created but no parts have been uploaded yet.
* ***ongoing***: Data upload is ongoing.
* ***completed***: Data upload has been successfully completed.
* ***failed***: Data upload has failed.

Data parts can be uploaded only if the upload state is one of the following: ***pending***, ***ongoing***, ***failed***. 
Note that the state will be changed to ***failed*** if uploading a part fails, 
but if the part is uploaded again successfully, the upload state is changed back to ***ongoing***.

The data can be downloaded only if the upload state is ***completed***.


## Creates a new data upload

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/largedata/v4 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Description for my large data",
    "name": "My large data"
  }'
```

`POST /largedata/v4`

Creates a new multipart large data upload.  Response contains `dataId`, which is the created large data object identifier.

## Completes data upload

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/largedata/v4/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /largedata/v4/{dataId}`

After all parts have been uploaded, this operation completes the upload.

When the upload has been completed, it is no longer possible to upload
new parts to it but the uploaded data can be downloaded.

This request has an optional `abort` query
parameter (the default value is `false`) for aborting the upload instead
of successfully completing it. If the upload is aborted, all of its
parts and data are removed from HERE Tracking.


<h3 id="completes-data-upload-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|abort|query|boolean|false|none|
|dataId|path|string|true|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

## Gets large data object

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/largedata/v4/string/data \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /largedata/v4/{dataId}/data`

Downloads a part of large data.

The data to be downloaded is identified with `dataId`. 
`offset` query paremeter specifies the first byte of the data,
and `count` indicates how many bytes of the data is to be downloaded
starting from and including the `offset`. The default value for `offset`
is zero and the for `count` it is the total size of the data.

The size of one downloaded data part must be between 1 byte and 10 MB.

## Uploads a part of a large data

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/largedata/v4/string/parts/1 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  --data-binary '@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /largedata/v4/{dataId}/parts/{partNumber}`

Uploads a part of large data. The part is identified with `dataId` and a part number.

Part upload has the following limits:
* The part numbers must start from 1, be no greater than 10000 and be consecutive.
* The size of one uploaded data part must be between 1 byte and 1 MB.
* Parts re-uploaded with the same `partNumber` are overridden.
* Only `application/octet-stream` Content-Type is supported.

Parts can be uploaded in any order, the `partNumber` determines their
position in the total data.

The optional `md5` query parameter can be used to provide the MD5
digest for the uploaded data part. If it is specified and does not match
to the received data, HERE Tracking returns HTTP status 400.

If the data upload is still in ***preparing*** state, HERE Tracking
returns HTTP status 409.


<h3 id="uploads-a-part-of-a-large-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|md5|query|string|false|none|
|dataId|path|string|true|none|
|partNumber|path|integer|true|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|body|body|string(binary)|false|none|

<h1 id="here-tracking-registry">Registry</h1>

The Registry service is used for provisioning and claiming devices.

Device licenses can only be provisioned by a vendor.
A vendor is a user who has a developer plan (evaluation or paid commercial) with HERE
that has been enabled for device license creation.
A user claiming a device is the device owner, which is different from the device vendor.
Access to the data generated by the device is limited to the device owner only.

## Claims a device

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/registry/v2/devices/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ownerAppId": "stringst"
  }'
```

`PUT /registry/v2/devices/{deviceOrExternalId}`

Claims a device, associating a device to a user account.
The user who claimed a device is the device owner,
which is different from the device vendor.

Unclaimed devices cannot login or send any data to HERE Tracking.
A claimed device data is stored in HERE Tracking and is available to the
device owner's project, which the device has been claimed to.

When a device is claimed, it gets assigned a `trackingId`.
This is a unique ID associated with the device data in HERE Tracking.

`trackingId` is different from the `deviceId`.
The `deviceId` is permanently associated with the hardware, while the `trackingId`
is associated with the device data.
If the device is later sold or transferred, the `deviceId` remains the same but the
`trackingId` changes in case the device is reclaimed.
This way the new owner cannot access the old data.

If the user is a member of multiple projects, the target project ID needs to be
specified in the `projectId` query parameter (note that this is different from the `appId`).

Only users with a valid HERE Tracking license are authorized to claim
new devices. Claimed devices are associated with the owner
application ID, and the total device count is kept up-to-date for billing purposes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ownerAppId": "stringst"
}
```

<h3 id="claims-a-device-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|deviceOrExternalId|path|string|true|Device ID of a provisioned physical device or for virtual devices an application specific external ID provided together with `appId` query parameter.|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ownerAppId|body|string|false|(Deprecated) Application identifier which specifies device owner's application to which the device is associated with.|

```json
}
```

## Deactivates a device.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/registry/v2/devices/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /registry/v2/devices/{deviceOrExternalId}`

Deactivates a provisioned device.
This operation will deactivate the device license (`deviceId` and `deviceSecret`).
Deactivated devices cannot be claimed anymore.

NOTE: The device must be unclaimed before it can be deactivated.

## Creates licenses for multiple devices

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/registry/v2/stringst/devices \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "count": 10
  }'
```

`POST /registry/v2/{appId}/devices`

Starts a batch job to create licenses for either physical devices or
virtual devices. Virtual devices are meant for cloud-to-cloud use case.

A physical device license is a `deviceId` and `deviceSecret` credential pair. The batch
job creates a number of physical device licenses specified by the `count`
parameter in the request body.
The response contains an array of `deviceId` and `deviceSecret` pairs.

Virtual devices are identified with an external device ID and the requestor's
project `appId`. The virtual device external ID is application-specific
and the user is free to allocate it as user finds suitable.
The external IDs for the virtual devices to be created are specified
in the `devices` array in request body. For virtual devices
the response contains only an array of `deviceId`s, but no `deviceSecret`s.

The `autoclaim` parameter can only be used when creating virtual devices.
If `autoclaim`=`true`, the created virtual devices are immediately claimed
by the requesting user account. In this case the response contains also
tracking IDs for the claimed devices.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "count": 10
}
```

<h3 id="creates-licenses-for-multiple-devices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|appId|path|string|true|Project appId of the user's project|
|autoclaim|query|boolean|false|If set to `true`, the licenses are created and devices are immediately claimed by the same user. Supported only with `deviceId` array in body, and not with the `count` parameter.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» count|body|integer|true|Number of device credentials requested|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» devices|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The external ID for the device|

> Example responses

> 202 Response

```json
{
  "jobId": "344a17a4-1b19-4420-bb6f-8400b87071fd"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json

  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 401,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 401306
  },
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The provided credentials are not valid."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 403,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 403306
  },
  "error": "Forbidden",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The account does not have the correct privileges."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
[
  {
    "code": 401,
    "details": {
      "hereErrorCode": 401306
    },
    "error": "Unauthorized",
```

## Unclaims a device

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/registry/v2/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /registry/v2/{trackingId}`

Unclaims a device removing the ownership association between the user and the device. The device data will no longer be accessible to the user. The device can then be reclaimed by a different or the same user.

|---|---|---|---|---|

|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

```json
}
```

<h1 id="here-tracking-aliases">Aliases</h1>


An alias is an arbitrary `type` - `externalId` pair, which can be associated with a `trackingId`.

The `externalId` can be, for example, an external management system asset ID or a human-readable name.
An alias is uniquely identified by an `externalId` and a `type` pair within a tracking project.


## Gets all aliases

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/aliases/v2 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /aliases/v2`

Gets all aliases of a project.

If `type` query parameter is provided, the response will contain
only aliases of the given type.

If `externalId` query parameter is specified, the
response will contain only aliases that match the given
external ID. The following wildcards can be used:
'*' matches any number of any characters,
'?' matches a single character.

If `after` query parameter is provided, the successful response will only
contain aliases that were created after the specified timestamp.
Parameters `after` and `pageToken` are mutually exclusive and cannot be provided at the same time.

The returned results are sorted in ascending order by the alias creation time.


<h3 id="gets-all-aliases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|count|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|after|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 0 to the current time.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|type|query|string|false|An alias type|
|externalId|query|string|false|Filter for aliases external IDs|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "aliases": {
        "cargoId": [
          "123-456"
        ],
        "engines": [
          "de7a0e9a-2e86-11e8-b20f-6c400892e894",
          "dfee3968-2e86-11e8-b4e0-6c400892e894"
        ]
      },
      "trackingId": "HERE-c47c0d1d-89fd-4961-b341-3eb109f58d19"
    },
    {
      "aliases": {
        "engines": [
          "5219bfc6-9779-4901-922a-e53a7c01037e"
        ]
      },
      "trackingId": "HERE-6da0f871-b4eb-4800-90e6-4bae86a788d6"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Deletes all aliases of a device

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/aliases/v2/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'x-confirm: true'
```

`DELETE /aliases/v2/{trackingId}`

Deletes all aliases of a device identified by the `trackingId`.

Note that one needs to supply an HTTP header `x-confirm` with the value `true` to force the deletion. 
If the header is not provided, the request will fail.


<h3 id="deletes-all-aliases-of-a-device-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-confirm|header|string|true|A safety measure that prevents one from accidentally deleting data.<br><br>To confirm that all entries should be deleted, set the value to `true`.<br>|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

<h1 id="here-tracking-associations">Associations</h1>

An association is a link between a device and a geofence, a sensor rule or a rule.
Device events get generated for existing associations only.

## Associates a device to a geofence

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/associations/v3/string/geofences/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /associations/v3/{trackingId}/geofences/{geofenceId}`

Associates the device with `trackingId` to the geofence with `geofenceId`.
Whenever the device enters or exits the associated geofence, an event is generated.


<h3 id="associates-a-device-to-a-geofence-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|geofenceId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the geofence|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
```

## Associates a device with a sensor rule

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/associations/v3/string/sensors/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /associations/v3/{trackingId}/sensors/{sensorRuleId}`

Associates the device with `trackingId` to the sensor rule with `sensorRuleId`.

A single device can only have one sensor rule per sensor type associated.

The associated sensor rule settings will be automatically synchronised to the `system.sensorAlarmConfig` section of the device
`desired shadow`.

Every time the associated sensor rule gets triggered by the device ingestion, an event will be generated.


<h3 id="associates-a-device-with-a-sensor-rule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|sensorRuleId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the sensor rule|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

<h1 id="here-tracking-bulk-jobs">Bulk jobs</h1>

deleting multiple devices at once.

## Starts bulk upload

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bulkjobs/v4/deviceUploads \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "areaBased": false,
      "distanceM": 0,
      "geofences": [
        "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
      ],
      "name": "string",
      "rules": [
        "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
      ],
      "sampleMs": 0,
      "sendMs": 0,
      "tags": [
        "string"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /bulkjobs/v4/deviceUploads`

Starts bulk upload process


> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "areaBased": false,
    "distanceM": 0,
    "geofences": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "name": "string",
    "rules": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "sampleMs": 0,
    "sendMs": 0,
    "tags": [
      "string"
    ],
    "type": "string"
  }
]
```

## Updates bulk upload job status

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/bulkjobs/v4/deviceUploads/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "action": "cancel"
  }'
```

`PATCH /bulkjobs/v4/deviceUploads/{jobId}`

Updates bulk upload status. In case current status is pending or ongoing, user can perform action `cancel`,
which cancels the bulk upload processes of the job that are still in the pending state.
In case current status is completed, failed or cancelled, user can perform action `acknowledged`
which can be used to mark the job acknowledged.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "cancel"
}
```

<h3 id="updates-bulk-upload-job-status-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|jobId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» action|body|string|true|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|cancel|
|» action|acknowledge|

```json
  "status": "pending"
}
```

<h1 id="here-tracking-c2c">C2C</h1>

The Cloud to Cloud service is used to create and manage connections between external
cloud providers and HERE Tracking.
A connection is formed by creating a cloud-to-cloud connector which receives reports from
the external cloud devices and transforms them into the HERE Tracking ingestions,
thus enabling the external devices to be tracked by HERE Tracking.


## Receives external device update reports

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/c2c/v4/callback?apiKey=string' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /c2c/v4/callback`

External clouds can call this endpoint through their callback mechanism
to report device updates. The format of the payload is driver specific.

## Creates a connector

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/c2c/v4/connectors \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "driverId": "my-driver-1-id",
    "enabled": true,
    "externalCloudInfo": {
      "extAppId": "ext-app-id",
      "extUserId": "ext-user-id",
      "extUserPassword": "ext-user-password"
    },
    "name": "driver-name",
    "refreshIntervalS": 3600
  }'
```

`POST /c2c/v4/connectors`

Registers a cloud-to-cloud connector between the HERE Tracking project `projectId`
and an external cloud using the cloud-to-cloud driver `driverId`
and the external cloud access credentials.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "driverId": "my-driver-1-id",
  "enabled": true,
  "externalCloudInfo": {
    "extAppId": "ext-app-id",
    "extUserId": "ext-user-id",
    "extUserPassword": "ext-user-password"
  },
  "name": "driver-name",
  "refreshIntervalS": 3600
}
```

|» externalCloudInfo|body|object|true|An external cloud-specific object that the driver will use to login to the<br>external cloud. The structure of this object varies per driver<br>implementation.<br>It is recommended to have dedicated credentials for logging in to<br>the external cloud in order not to violate possible concurrent users<br>policies of the external cloud.<br>In case of the HERE Tracking loopback driver, the maximum<br>allowed concurrent user account tokens is 3 per account,<br>therefore it is recommended to create a separate HERE account<br>and grant it the required privilege to update the connector's<br>project, and use that account in externalCloudInfo.<br>|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connectorId|string|false|none|Identifier of the connector.|
|projectId|string|false|none|Project ID.<br>Any HERE Tracking user must be a member of a Tracking project.<br>The project ID can be implicitly resolved if the user calling the API is a member of a single project.<br>If the user is a member of multiple projects, the `projectId` query parameter needs to be specified explicitly.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|Brief description of the connector.|
|driverId|string|true|none|Identifier of the driver to be used with this connector.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Enabled state of the connector. If set to false then the connector<br>will not execute periodically.<br>|
|externalCloudInfo|object|true|none|An external cloud-specific object that the driver will use to login to the<br>external cloud. The structure of this object varies per driver<br>implementation.<br>It is recommended to have dedicated credentials for logging in to<br>the external cloud in order not to violate possible concurrent users<br>policies of the external cloud.<br>In case of the HERE Tracking loopback driver, the maximum<br>allowed concurrent user account tokens is 3 per account,<br>therefore it is recommended to create a separate HERE account<br>and grant it the required privilege to update the connector's<br>project, and use that account in externalCloudInfo.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the connector.|
|refreshIntervalS|integer|false|none|This is the interval (in seconds) to execute the sync process<br>between the connector's external cloud and HERE Tracking project.<br>The maximum and at the same time default value for callback-type connectors is 900 seconds.<br>The default value for other type of connectors is 3600 seconds and there is no maximum value set.<br>|
|lastExecTs|string|false|none|Timestamp of the last connection execution.|
|totalAddedDevices|integer|true|none|Number of external devices added to the connector.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the connector creation.|

<h1 id="here-tracking-events">Events</h1>

The Events service manages device and shipment events.

An event is created every time an associated rule or geofence is triggered by a device ingestion. 

A geofence event is created every time a device enters or exits an associated geofence.
A sensor event is created when sensor data reported by a device triggers a sensor rule. 
A rule event (such as dwelling, detention, utilization, stock and online rule) is created when
a device behaviour triggers a rule.


## Gets event history

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/events/v3 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events/v3`

Gets all events for all devices and shipments of the project. The results are listed in descending order 
based on the timestamp. 

An event is uniquely identified by `trackingId`-`ruleId`-`timestamp` key, 
with an exception of dwelling and stock rule events. 
Dwelling events also need `geofenceId` to be specified, 
whereas for stock events `trackingId` is not applicable.

A time range can be defined with `before` and `after` timestamps. The response will contain
an array of events that were recorded within the range.

If the request is supplied with `eventSource` query parameter, the response will contain
events generated by the defined source only.

If the request is supplied with `eventType` query parameter, the response will contain
events of the specified type only.

If the request is supplied with `ruleId` query parameter, the response will only contain events
for the specified rule ID.

If the request is supplied with `initialState` query parameter, the response will contain
events having the specified initial state.

All the aforementioned query parameters can be combined together.


<h3 id="gets-event-history-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|before|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 1 to the current time.<br>|
|after|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 0 to the current time.<br>|
|eventSource|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|eventType|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|ruleId|query|string(uuid) \| [string(uuid)]|false|none|
|initialState|query|boolean|false|none|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|count|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

```json
    {
      "eventSource": "attach",
      "eventType": "TRUE_TO_FALSE",
```

## Gets the event statuses

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/events/v3/statuses \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events/v3/statuses`

Gets all events statuses for all devices and shipments of the project.
An event status of a device is the most recent event of any rule or geofence the device 
is associated with.
The same applies for shipments.

The response contains a list of event status objects and
each object has the following properties:
* `trackingId` or `shipmentId`: a device ID or a shipment ID
* `ruleId`: an associated rule or geofence ID
* `eventSource`: the rule type
* `eventType`: an event type of the latest event of the rule (same as the "event state")
* `timestamp`: a time since when the device has been in this event state

The array is sorted by the following fields in the
following order: `trackingId`, `eventSource`, `timestamp`, `ruleId`, `geofenceId`.

A time range can be defined with `before` and `after` timestamps. The response will contain
event statuses that were recorded within the range.

If the request is supplied with `eventSource` query parameter, the response results will be limited
to the specified rule types only.

If the request is supplied with `ruleId` query parameter, the response results will be limited
to the specified rule IDs only.

If the request is supplied with `trackingId` query parameter, the response results will be limited
to the specified devices only. Also `shipmentId` can be used as a `trackingId`.

If the request is supplied with `eventType` query parameter, the response results will be limited
to the specified type only.

If the request is supplied with `geofenceId` query parameter, it will only affect dwelling 
event statuses filtering, limiting the results to the specified geofence only.
Other event types are not affected by this setting.
Note that for the event statuses of geofence type, the `ruleId` is the `geofenceId`.

If the request is supplied with `shipments` query parameter, the response results will be limited
either to shipments (`shipments`=`true`) or devices (`shipments`=`false`) only. 
Otherwise, if `shipments` query parameter is not specified, response results will include both devices and shipments.

All the aforementioned query parameters can be combined together.


<h3 id="gets-the-event-statuses-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|eventSource|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|eventType|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|trackingId|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|ruleId|query|string(uuid) \| [string(uuid)]|false|none|
|geofenceId|query|string(uuid) \| [string(uuid)]|false|none|
|shipments|query|boolean|false|none|
|before|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 1 to the current time.<br>|
|after|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 0 to the current time.<br>|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|count|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

## Gets the number of devices and shipments in each event state

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/events/v3/statuses/deviceCounts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events/v3/statuses/deviceCounts`

This API call counts the number of devices and shipments that are currently in the different 
event states per rule or per event source (that is per rule type).

An event state of a device is the event type of the most recent device event.
It indicates a state the device is currently in, in relation to a rule the device is associated with.

For example, the event state can be either `INSIDE_GEOFENCE` or `OUTSIDE_GEOFENCE` in case the event source is `geofence`; 
or `BELOW_RANGE`, `IN_RANGE` or `ABOVE_RANGE` in case the event source is `battery` rule.

A device can be in several different event states at the same time when it has more than 
one rule associated with it. 
For example, a device can be at the same time in `INSIDE_GEOFENCE` and `ABOVE_RANGE` event states.

The same applies for shipments.

The `groupBy` query parameter defines how the results are grouped.

The default value for the `groupBy` parameter is `ruleId`. 
The response contains a list of objects, one per each rule,
that are associated to at least one device or shipment of the project.
Each object has the following properties:
* `ruleId`: a rule ID
* `eventSource`: the rule type
* every distinct event state (applicable for the rule type) and the number of devices in this state
* `total`: the total number of devices associated to the rule

When the `groupBy` parameter value is `eventSource`, the response contains a list of objects, one per
event source (that is per each rule type),
that are associated to at least one device or shipment of the project.
Each object has the following properties:
* `eventSource`: a rule type
* every distinct event state (applicable for the rule type) and the number of devices in this state. 
  One device is counted only once per `eventType` state, but in case a single device is associated to multiple
  rules of the same type, it will be counted separately for each event state.
* `total`: the total number of devices associated to the rule type. A single device is counted only once.

For example, a device A is associated to 2 geofences and is inside one and outside the other.
A device B is associated to 3 geofences and is outside all of them. With the request 
query parameter set as `groupBy`=`eventSource`, the response body will contain the following result item:
```
{
  "eventSource": "geofence",
  "INSIDE_GEOFENCE": 1,
  "OUTSIDE_GEOFENCE": 2,
  "total": 2
}.
```

If the request is supplied with `eventSource` query parameter, the response results will be limited
to the specified rule types only.

If the request is supplied with `ruleId` query parameter, the response results will be limited
to the specified rule IDs only.

If the request is supplied with `trackingId` query parameter, the response results will be limited
to the specified devices only. Also `shipmentId` can be used as a `trackingId`.

If the request is supplied with `geofenceId` query parameter, it will only affect dwelling 
event statuses filtering, limiting the results to the specified geofence only.
Other event types are not affected by this setting.
Note that for the event statuses of geofence type, the `ruleId` is the `geofenceId`.

If the request is supplied with `shipments` query parameter, the response results will be limited
either to shipments (`shipments`=`true`) or devices (`shipments`=`false`) only. 
Otherwise, if `shipments` query parameter is not specified, response results will include both devices and shipments.

All the aforementioned query parameters can be combined together.

## Gets event history for a device or a shipment

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/events/v3/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events/v3/{trackingId}`

Gets all events for a device or a shipment. 
A device is identified by the `trackingId`.
For shipments, `shipmentId` can be used as a `trackingId`.

The results are listed in descending order based on the timestamp.

An event is uniquely identified by `trackingId`-`ruleId`-`timestamp` key, 
with an exception of dwelling and stock rule events. 
Dwelling events also need `geofenceId` to be specified, 
whereas for stock events `trackingId` is not applicable.

A single event can be fetched using `ruleId`, `before` and `after` query parameters.

A time range can be defined with `before` and `after` timestamps. The response will contain
an array of events that were recorded within the range.

If the request is supplied with `eventSource` query parameter, the response will contain
events generated by the defined source only.

If the request is supplied with `eventType` query parameter, the response will contain
events of the specified type only.

If the request is supplied with `ruleId` query parameter, the response will only contain events
for the specified rule ID.

If the request is supplied with `initialState` query parameter, the response will contain
events having the specified initial state.

All the aforementioned query parameters can be combined together.


<h3 id="gets-event-history-for-a-device-or-a-shipment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|before|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 1 to the current time.<br>|
|after|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 0 to the current time.<br>|
|eventSource|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|eventType|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|ruleId|query|string(uuid) \| [string(uuid)]|false|none|
|initialState|query|boolean|false|none|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|count|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|

<h1 id="here-tracking-geofence-associations">Geofence Associations</h1>

This service is used to manage associations between devices and geofences.
When a device enters or exits an associated geofence, an event gets generated.

> **IMPORTANT**
> Geofence Associations v2 API is deprecated. Please use Associations v3 API instead.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofence-associations/v2/health \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Associates a device with a geofence

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofence-associations/v2/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /geofence-associations/v2/{geofenceId}/{trackingId}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Associates the device with `trackingId` to the geofence with `geofenceId`. 
Whenever the device enters or exits the associated geofence, an event is generated.

|geofenceId|path|string(uuid)|true|Geofence ID|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

## Disassociates a device and a geofence

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofence-associations/v2/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /geofence-associations/v2/{geofenceId}/{trackingId}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Deletes an association between the geofence `geofenceId` and the device `trackingId`.


<h3 id="disassociates-a-device-and-a-geofence-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

<h1 id="here-tracking-geofences">Geofences</h1>

The Geofences service creates and manages geofences.

A geofence is an area boundary that users can define and associate with their devices.
The area that the geofence encloses can be defined using geographic coordinates or radio measurements.

Geographic geofences can be `circular` or `polygonal`. 
A circular geofence is defined by geographic coordinates of its center and a radius, 
while polygonal geofences are defined as a set of geographic coordinates.

`POI geofence` (Point Of Interest) is a geofence, which is defined using radio measurements.
POI geofences need to be trained separately using a telemetry that a device has recorded while 
being at the desired point of interest. 

Once created, a geofence can be associated to a device. 
Every time a position or a radio measurement update is received from a device, 
HERE Tracking would evaluate whether the device has transitioned across the boundary of 
an associated geofence.
If such a transition has happened, a transition event will be recorded.
For the geographic geofences, the evaluation is based on the coordinates of the trace.
For POI geofences, the device is considered to be inside a trained POI geofence when the radio 
measurements of the device-ingested telemetry and the training data match.

Indoor geofences can be created by adding the floor properties to the geofence definition.
Circular and polygonal geofences can be both outdoors and indoors. 
POI geofences should only be used indoors.
For indoor geofences a device transition is recorded only if the position of the device is indoors 
and the floor details of the position match the geofence floor definition.

NOTE: A geofence can also be referred to as a geozone, and these two terms are interchangeable.


## Gets all geofences

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofences/v2 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /geofences/v2`

Gets all geofences of a project. 
Results can be filtered by using the query parameters.
Indoor geofences with the `floor` properties
may be filtered by `floor[id]`, which specifies the ID of the venue associated with the geofence.

|type|query|[string]|false|Type of a geofence|
|bbox|query|[number]|false|Limit search to geofences intersecting the given bounding box.|

|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|

## Creates a geofence

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofences/v2 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "definition": {
      "center": {
        "lat": -90,
        "lng": -180
      },
      "floor": {
        "id": "string",
        "level": -999,
        "name": "string"
      },
      "radius": 0
    },
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "type": "circle"
  }'
```

`POST /geofences/v2`

One can specify a geofence as a circle, as a polygon or as POI (Point of Interest). One can also
assign a name and a description to each geofence to help identify them.

Circle
---

Specify coordinates of the center point of the circle and a radius in
meters.

```json
    {
      "name": "Home",
      "type": "circle",
      "definition": {
        "center": {
          "lat": 52.5308398,
          "lng": 13.38490035
        },
        "radius": 100
      },
      "description": "Small area around my house."
    }
```

Polygon
---

Specify an array of points. A minimum of three points is required.

*NOTE: If the array of points does not describe a closed polygon, the polygon is
automatically closed between the last and first points.*

```json
    {
      "name": "Work",
      "type": "polygon",
      "definition": {
        "points": [{
          "lat": 52.5308398,
          "lng": 13.38490035
        }, {
          "lat": 52.530443,
          "lng": 13.38482003
        }, {
          "lat": 52.5308298,
          "lng": 13.38492235
        }]
      },
      "description": "The area around work."
    }
```

Indoor geofence
---

Circular and polygonal geofences can be both outdoors and indoors.
To create a `circular` `indoor` geofence, add the `floor` property to the request body.

```json
    {
      "name": "Office indoor",
      "type": "circle",
      "definition": {
        "center": {
          "lat": 52.5308398,
          "lng": 13.38490035
        },
        "radius": 20,
        "floor": {
          "level": 2,
          "id": "DM_1234",
          "name": "Office floor 2"
        }
      },
      "description": "Floor 2 of the office."
    }

```

POI geofence
---

Specify location details of a POI geofence for its initial creation.

After the POI geofence has been created, it will need to be trained.
The POI geofence boundary is defined using radio measurements.
The POI geofence is trained using a telemetry 
that a device has ingested while being at this desired point of interest.

For a trained POI geofence, an associated device is considered to be inside the 
geofence when the radio measurements of the device-ingested telemetry and 
the training data match.

```json
    {
      "name": "POI room in the office",
      "type": "poi",
      "definition": {
        "location": {
          "room": ROOM_201,
          "address": Invalidenstrasse 116,
          "country": Germany,
          "position": {
            "lat": 52.5308398,
            "lng": 13.38490035
          }
        },
        "floor": {
          "level": 2,
          "id": "DM_1234",
          "name": "Office floor 2"
        }
      },
      "description": "A room where goods should be delivered."
    }
```

Successful requests have the HTTP status 201 and the response body provides
the ID of the created geofence.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "definition": {
    "center": {
      "lat": -90,
      "lng": -180
    },
    "floor": {
      "id": "string",
      "level": -999,
      "name": "string"
    },
    "radius": 0
  },
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "type": "circle"
}
```

## Deletes all geofences

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofences/v2 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'x-confirm: true'
```

`DELETE /geofences/v2`

Deletes all geofences of a project.

If a geofence is associated with a stock rule, the rule will also be deleted.

Note that one needs to supply an HTTP header `x-confirm` with the value `true` to force the deletion. 
If the header is not provided, the request will fail.


<h3 id="deletes-all-geofences-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-confirm|header|string|true|A safety measure that prevents one from accidentally deleting data.<br><br>To confirm that all entries should be deleted, set the value to `true`.<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|x-confirm|true|

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

```json
  },
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
```

```json
  "message": "The account does not have the correct privileges."
}
```
