## Checks if a POI geofence training is possible with the given parameters

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofences/v2/trainingTest \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "after": 0,
    "before": 0,
    "id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /geofences/v2/trainingTest`

Checks if a POI geofence training is possible with the given request parameters.

The request body contains a training data sample in form of either a device tracking ID 
along with a specific time range for the ingested device telemetry or a WLAN scan.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "after": 0,
  "before": 0,
  "id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="checks-if-a-poi-geofence-training-is-possible-with-the-given-parameters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» after|body|integer|true|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The value must be within the past 24 hours from the current timestamp<br>|
|» before|body|integer|true|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The value must not be greater than current timestamp<br>|
|» id|body|string|true|This is a unique ID associated with the device data in HERE Tracking. For physical devices the `trackingId` gets assigned to a device when the device is claimed by a user, and for virtual devices it is an external device ID along with the device project `appId`.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» wlan|body|[object]|true|WLAN access points|
|» » band|body|number|false|Frequency range (GHz). Allowed values are 2.4, 3.65, and 5. (Possible future values include 4.9, 5.9, 60, and 900.)|
|» » mac|body|string|true|The MAC address of the WLAN access point. MAC-48 address with colon (:) or hyphen (-) separators, upper or lower case hex digits. Note that if the SSID contains postfix '_nomap', the AP should not be used for positioning. For privacy reasons positioning based on a single WLAN AP is not possible; there has to be at least one other matching wlan or cell.|
|» » powrx|body|integer|true|Received signal level (dBm) at the terminal (Optional)|
|» » timestamp|body|string(date-time)|false|Time of the wlan measurement (UTC) (Optional)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » band|2.4|
|» » band|3.65|
|» » band|5|

## Updates a single geofence

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofences/v2/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "definition": {
      "center": {
        "lat": -90,
        "lng": -180
      },
      "floor": {
        "id": "string",
        "level": -999,
        "name": "string"
      },
      "radius": 0
    },
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "type": "circle"
  }'
```

`PUT /geofences/v2/{geofenceId}`

Updates the geofence `type`, `name`, `description` or `definition` property. 
The old geofence will be replaced by the new one, and hence the full set of the 
geofence properties must be provided in the request body. 
`POI` geofence type cannot be changed to `circle` or `polygon` and vice versa.

If the update was successful, the response will contain the updated geofence details.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "definition": {
    "center": {
      "lat": -90,
      "lng": -180
    },
    "floor": {
      "id": "string",
      "level": -999,
      "name": "string"
    },
    "radius": 0
  },
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "type": "circle"
}
```

## Trains a POI geofence

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/geofences/v2/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/poiTraining \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "after": 0,
    "before": 0,
    "id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /geofences/v2/{geofenceId}/poiTraining`

Trains the POI geofence `geofenceId` using a device telemetry.
The POI geofence boundary is defined using radio measurements.
The geofence is trained using a telemetry that the device with `trackingId` has ingested 
during the specified time range, while being at this point of interest.
Only telemetries that have been ingested during the last 24 hours can be used in the training.

Optionally, a WLAN scan be used for the training.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "after": 0,
  "before": 0,
  "id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="trains-a-poi-geofence-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|geofenceId|path|string(uuid)|true|ID of the geofence|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» after|body|integer|true|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The value must be within the past 24 hours from the current timestamp<br>|
|» before|body|integer|true|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The value must not be greater than current timestamp<br>|
|» id|body|string|true|This is a unique ID associated with the device data in HERE Tracking. For physical devices the `trackingId` gets assigned to a device when the device is claimed by a user, and for virtual devices it is an external device ID along with the device project `appId`.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» wlan|body|[object]|true|WLAN access points|
|» » band|body|number|false|Frequency range (GHz). Allowed values are 2.4, 3.65, and 5. (Possible future values include 4.9, 5.9, 60, and 900.)|
|» » mac|body|string|true|The MAC address of the WLAN access point. MAC-48 address with colon (:) or hyphen (-) separators, upper or lower case hex digits. Note that if the SSID contains postfix '_nomap', the AP should not be used for positioning. For privacy reasons positioning based on a single WLAN AP is not possible; there has to be at least one other matching wlan or cell.|
|» » powrx|body|integer|true|Received signal level (dBm) at the terminal (Optional)|
|» » timestamp|body|string(date-time)|false|Time of the wlan measurement (UTC) (Optional)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » band|2.4|
|» » band|3.65|
|» » band|5|

<h1 id="here-tracking-labels">Labels</h1>

The Labels service creates and manages labels.

A label is a key-value pair that can be associated to the following resources:

* device
* geofence
* sensor
* rule
* location
* shipment

One can list labels for a specific resource or resource type, and filter
labels by keys or key-value pairs.

## Gets all labels of a resource type

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/labels/v4/device \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /labels/v4/{resourceType}`

Gets all labels of the resource type `resourceType` within a project.

The `fields` parameter specifies which fields should be added to the response body 
(for example, `resourceId`).

The `labels` query parameter is specified as a label filter, and only the matching
results will be returned:

"?labels[priority]=high&labels[group]=group1&fields=resourceId,labels"
"?labels[group]=*"


<h3 id="gets-all-labels-of-a-resource-type-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|labels|query|object|false|A filter containing label key-value pairs.|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page|
|fields|query|[string]|false|Field names to filter a result object.<br>|
|resourceType|path|string|true|The resource type, for example "device", "geofence".|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|resourceType|device|
|resourceType|geofence|
|resourceType|location|
|resourceType|rule|
|resourceType|sensorRule|
|resourceType|shipment|

<h1 id="here-tracking-locations">Locations</h1>

The Locations service creates and manages locations.

This is an Alpha version of the Locations API and can still be changed in future releases.

Locations are geographical points of interest users may store in HERE Tracking. Locations are
used as building blocks for shipments.


## Gets all locations

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/locations/v4 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /locations/v4`

Gets all locations of the project.


<h3 id="gets-all-locations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|geofenceId|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter the results by `geofenceId`|
|name|query|string|false|Filter locations by name. Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|street|query|string|false|Filter locations by street address. Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|city|query|string|false|Filter locations by city. Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|postalCode|query|string|false|Filter locations by postal code. Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|state|query|string|false|Filter locations by state. Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|country|query|string|false|Filter locations by country. Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|locationId|query|string|false|Filter locations by locationId wildcard.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|sort|query|string \| [string]|false|A paramater to specify field to sort by and order.<br>The following format can be used:<br>'name:asc' sort by name in ascending order,<br>'steet:desc' sort by street in descending order.<br>Allowed fields to sort by:<br>locationId, name, street, city, postalCode, state, country.<br>|
|externalLocationId|query|string|false|Filter locations by external location id|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

## Creates a location

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/locations/v4 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Rostock Port Hafenbecken C",
    "geofenceId": "57713e50-194e-4803-8ca6-1e794e916094",
    "location": {
      "lat": 54.155147,
      "lng": 12.12204
    },
    "name": "Rostock Port"
  }'
```

`POST /locations/v4`

Creates a new location.
A location consists of latitude/longitude coordinate pair and/or geofenceId.
A name, description, and address of the location may be provided.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Rostock Port Hafenbecken C",
  "geofenceId": "57713e50-194e-4803-8ca6-1e794e916094",
  "location": {
    "lat": 54.155147,
    "lng": 12.12204
  },
  "name": "Rostock Port"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-location-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» address|body|object|false|Location address.|
|» » city|body|string|false|City|
|» » country|body|string|false|Country|
|» » postalCode|body|string|false|Postal code|
|» » state|body|string|false|State|
|» » street|body|string|false|Street address|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the location.|
|» externalLocationId|body|string|false|External location id in external cloud|
|» geofenceId|body|string(uuid)|false|Optional geofence ID associated with the location. A geofence with the specified ID must exist.|
|» location|body|object|false|Location coordinates.|
|» » lat|body|number|true|Latitude in WGS-84 format, decimal representation ranging from -90 to 90.|
|» » lng|body|number|true|Longitude in WGS-84 format, decimal representation ranging from -180 to 180.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the location.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

```json
  "locationId": "string"
}
```

```json
}
```

## Deletes all locations

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/locations/v4 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'x-confirm: true'
```

`DELETE /locations/v4`

Deletes all locations of the project.

Note that one needs to supply an HTTP header `x-confirm` with the value `true` to force the deletion.
If the header is not provided, the request will fail.


<h3 id="deletes-all-locations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-confirm|header|string|true|A safety measure that prevents one from accidentally deleting data.<br><br>To confirm that all entries should be deleted, set the value to `true`.<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

|---|---|
|x-confirm|true|

## Updates a location details

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/locations/v4/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Rostock Port Hafenbecken C",
    "geofenceId": "57713e50-194e-4803-8ca6-1e794e916094",
    "location": {
      "lat": 54.155147,
      "lng": 12.12204
    },
    "name": "Rostock Port"
  }'
```

`PUT /locations/v4/{locationId}`

Updates the location `locationId` details. A location consists of latitude/longitude coordinate pair and/or geofenceId.
A name, description, and address of the location may be provided.
The old location definition will be replaced, meaning that
full location body should be provided. After a successful update, the response provides
the updated location details.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Rostock Port Hafenbecken C",
  "geofenceId": "57713e50-194e-4803-8ca6-1e794e916094",
  "location": {
    "lat": 54.155147,
    "lng": 12.12204
  },
  "name": "Rostock Port"
}
```

<h3 id="updates-a-location-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|locationId|path|string|true|Location ID|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» address|body|object|false|Location address.|
|» » city|body|string|false|City|
|» » country|body|string|false|Country|
|» » postalCode|body|string|false|Postal code|
|» » state|body|string|false|State|
|» » street|body|string|false|Street address|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the location.|
|» externalLocationId|body|string|false|External location id in external cloud|
|» geofenceId|body|string(uuid)|false|Optional geofence ID associated with the location. A geofence with the specified ID must exist.|
|» location|body|object|false|Location coordinates.|
|» » lat|body|number|true|Latitude in WGS-84 format, decimal representation ranging from -90 to 90.|
|» » lng|body|number|true|Longitude in WGS-84 format, decimal representation ranging from -180 to 180.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the location.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|

## Deletes a location

<h1 id="here-tracking-metadata">Metadata</h1>

The Metadata service creates and manages metadata.

Metadata is a descriptive information added to a device, a shipment, a geofence or a sensor rule.


## Gets a batch of metadata of multiple devices or shipments

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/metadata/v2/devices/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    "HERE-d0c29690-5d26-4cf1-a37e-b7816e72cb99",
    "SHP-ff92eda0-3114-4640-b7e6-4ba641ae1124"
  ]'
```

`POST /metadata/v2/devices/batch`

Gets a batch of metadata of multiple devices or shipments. The device or shipment IDs are specified in the request body.

```json

  "HERE-d0c29690-5d26-4cf1-a37e-b7816e72cb99",
```

## Creates or updates metadata of a device or a shipment

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/metadata/v2/devices/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "priority": "high"
  }'
```

`PUT /metadata/v2/devices/{trackingId}`

Updates the metadata object of the device or a shipment identified by the `trackingId` or the `shipmentId`. 
The metadata specified in the request body is merged with the existing metadata object 
(or gets created if no metadata object exists); 
new keys are added, and the values of the existing keys are updated with the new data.
Adding 'null' value for a key deletes it from the metadata object.
Successful response body contains the updated metadata object.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "priority": "high"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-or-updates-metadata-of-a-device-or-a-shipment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|body|body|object|true|Metadata object associated with the resource. Max size 1k.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "priority": "high"
  },
  "id": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

```json
}
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "priority": "high"
  }'
```

`PUT /metadata/v2/geofences/{geofenceId}`

Updates the metadata object of the geofence identified by the `geofenceId`. 
The metadata specified in the request body is merged with the existing metadata object 
(or gets created if no metadata object exists); 
new keys are added, and the values of the existing keys are updated with the new data.
Adding 'null' value for a key deletes it from the metadata object.
Successful response body contains the updated metadata object.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "priority": "high"
}
```

<h3 id="creates-or-updates-metadata-of-a-geofence-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|geofenceId|path|string(uuid)|true|Geofence ID|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|body|body|object|true|Metadata object associated with the resource. Max size 1k.|

<h1 id="here-tracking-notifications">Notifications</h1>

The Notifications service provides a way to manage notification channels.

Users need to register notification channels to get notified about new events.
The supported notification channel types are webhook, 
email and browser pull. Webhook notifications are common for all users in a project, but email and
browser pull notification subscriptions are user-specific. 

Email notifications will only be sent to a verified HERE Account email address.
The browser pull notifications will be enabled for the [HERE Tracking Asset web](https://asset.tracking.here.com).
For the webhook notifications, a URL registered as a webhook will receive a POST request on any
matching event occurence.

To get notified only about some specific events, users can apply various filters when subscribing to notifications, 
specifying, for example, a particular rule ID or a geofence ID.
If an occuring event matches `ruleId`, `eventSource`, `eventType` and `initialState` 
filter settings, a notification gets triggerred.

A single notification contains multiple matching event objects, for example:

```
[
  {
    "eventType": "ABOVE_RANGE",
    "ruleId": "a3f652bc-a456-7f12-cd11-123ah761yt41",
    "ruleName": "My temperature rule"
    "eventSource": "temperature"
    "trackingId": "HERE-871eb4c9-76f6-4e9d-bed7-fa114f793e83",
    "timestamp": 1499258184356,
    "initialState": false
  },
  {
    "eventType": "INSIDE_GEOFENCE",
    "ruleId": "e2f651ee-f196-4fa3-bf88-894dc131dea3",
    "ruleName": "Warehouse 12345"
    "eventSource": "geofence"
    "trackingId": "HERE-871eb4c9-76f6-4e9d-bed7-fa114f793e83",
    "timestamp": 1499258184356,
    "initialState": false
  },
  {
    "eventType": "DWELLING_STARTED",
    "ruleId": "bf4510c0-ffa1-4ae3-8174-6a3474f7091e",
    "ruleName": "Dwelling 1 hour in a geofence"
    "eventSource": "dwelling"
    "trackingId": "HERE-871eb4c9-76f6-4e9d-bed7-fa114f793e83",
    "timestamp": 1499258184356,
    "geofenceId": "e2f651ee-f196-4fa3-bf88-894dc131dea3",
    "geofenceName": "Warehouse 12345"
    "initialState": false
  }
]
```

If a device is offline, its notifications will not be sent to the user until the device is back online again.

## Updates a notification channel

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/v3/registration/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "channelType": "webhook",
    "eventSource": "attach",
    "eventType": "BELOW_RANGE",
    "initialState": true,
    "ruleId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "url": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /notifications/v3/registration/{channelId}`

Updates the `url`, `ruleId`, `eventSource`, `eventType` and `initialState` parameters of
the notification channel `channelId`. If a property is not provided in the request body,
its value will be updated to null. When updating a webhook channel, the `url` parameter must be provided.

After a successful update, the response provides the updated notification channel details.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "channelType": "webhook",
  "eventSource": "attach",
  "eventType": "BELOW_RANGE",
  "initialState": true,
  "ruleId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="updates-a-notification-channel-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|channelId|path|string(uuid)|true|The notification channel ID.<br>|
|body|body|object|true|Request body contains a notification channel registration information|
|» channelType|body|string|true|The type of notification channel.|
|» eventSource|body|string|false|The event source rule type.<br>|
|» eventType|body|string|false|Type of the event.<br><br>An event is created every time an associated rule or geofence is triggered by a device ingestion.<br>The event type depends on the data the device sends.<br><br>Sensors that report numerical data (such as battery, humidity, pressure and temperature sensors),<br>generate an event when the reported sensor reading of the device goes in or out of range, which is configured in the rule.<br>This produces events of BELOW_RANGE, IN_RANGE and ABOVE_RANGE types.<br><br>Sensors that report boolean data (such as attach and tamper sensors), generate events when the device <br>transitions from one state to another, either from `false` to `true` or vice versa.<br>This produces events of FALSE_TO_TRUE and TRUE_TO_FALSE types.<br>The same event types are also generated by the online rule when the device state changes from `offline` <br>(when the device has stopped ingesting data) to `online` (when the device data ingestion has resumed) <br>or vice versa.<br><br>The acceleration sensor generates events whenever the reported sensor reading <br>crosses the acceleration threshold (for example, when the device was dropped).<br>This produces events of the type EVENT. <br>Such events are stateless.<br><br>Events of INSIDE_GEOFENCE and OUTSIDE_GEOFENCE types are generated when the device enters or exits<br>a geofence associated with the device.<br><br>Events of DWELLING_STARTED type are generated when the device has<br>stayed inside an associated geofence for longer than the threshold duration. <br>DWELLING_ENDED type events are generated when dwelling of the device has ended.<br><br>Events of DETENTION_STARTED type are generated when the device has been<br>stationary for longer than the threshold duration, regardless whether the device is inside <br>or outside of any geofence. <br>DETENTION_ENDED type events will be generated when the device starts moving again.<br><br>Events of UNUTILIZED type are generated when the device has been stationary for longer than the<br>threshold duration.<br>UTILIZED type events are generated when the device starts moving again after having been stationary.<br><br>Events of OVERSTOCK, NORMAL_VOLUME and UNDERSTOCK types are generated when the number of assets<br>inside a geofence crosses the `minVolume` and `maxVolume` thresholds of an associated stock rule.<br><br>Events of SHIPMENT_EARLY, SHIPMENT_ON_TIME and SHIPMENT_DELAYED types are generated when a shipment<br>is too early, on time or delayed.<br>|
|» initialState|body|boolean|false|Events with the `initialState` property set as `true` are generated when the rule is <br>evaluated for the first time. It indicates the fact that this is the initial evaluation <br>state, which would serve as a starting point for the subsequent rule evaluations.<br>The rest of the rule events would represent a transition of a device or a shipment or <br>a geofence from one state to another and their `initialState` property will be set to `false`.<br>|
|» ruleId|body|string(uuid)|false|Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|» url|body|string|false|A webhook URL that will receive notifications POST requests.<br>|

## Unregisters from notifications

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/v3/registration/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /notifications/v3/registration/{channelId}`

|channelId|path|string(uuid)|true|The notification channel ID.<br>|

## Gets all registered notification channels

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/v3/registrations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /notifications/v3/registrations`

Gets a list of all registered notification channels.


<h3 id="gets-all-registered-notification-channels-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|count|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|channelType|query|[string]|false|Filter result by channelType.<br><br>Example: `channelType[]=webhook`, `channelType[]=browserPull,email`<br>|
|userId|query|string|false|User ID. Can be used by the project admin to filter email and browser pull notification channels by subscriber.<br>|
|emailBounce|query|boolean|false|Filters by `emailBounce` property. When set to `true`, returns the email channels which are not active anymore<br>due to email bounce. When set to `false`, returns all the channels which are active (and not only email channels).<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|channelType|webhook|
|channelType|email|
|channelType|browserPull|

|error|string|true|none|An HTTP error description|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|An error ID that allows you to trace the error details|
|message|string|false|none|Descriptive text that explains the error|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
Bearer
</aside>

## Registers for notifications

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/v3/registrations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "channelType": "webhook",
    "eventSource": "attach",
    "eventType": "BELOW_RANGE",
    "initialState": true,
    "ruleId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "url": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /notifications/v3/registrations`

User can subscribe to notifications of all events triggered by device telemetry and rules and geofences.

To get notified about some specific events only, one can set up `ruleId`, `eventSource`, `eventType` 
and `initialState` filters for a notification channel.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "channelType": "webhook",
  "eventSource": "attach",
  "eventType": "BELOW_RANGE",
  "initialState": true,
  "ruleId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "url": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="registers-for-notifications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|userId|query|string|false|User Id.<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|body|body|object|true|Request body contains registration information|
|» channelType|body|string|true|The type of notification channel.|
|» eventSource|body|string|false|The event source rule type.<br>|
|» eventType|body|string|false|Type of the event.<br><br>An event is created every time an associated rule or geofence is triggered by a device ingestion.<br>The event type depends on the data the device sends.<br><br>Sensors that report numerical data (such as battery, humidity, pressure and temperature sensors),<br>generate an event when the reported sensor reading of the device goes in or out of range, which is configured in the rule.<br>This produces events of BELOW_RANGE, IN_RANGE and ABOVE_RANGE types.<br><br>Sensors that report boolean data (such as attach and tamper sensors), generate events when the device <br>transitions from one state to another, either from `false` to `true` or vice versa.<br>This produces events of FALSE_TO_TRUE and TRUE_TO_FALSE types.<br>The same event types are also generated by the online rule when the device state changes from `offline` <br>(when the device has stopped ingesting data) to `online` (when the device data ingestion has resumed) <br>or vice versa.<br><br>The acceleration sensor generates events whenever the reported sensor reading <br>crosses the acceleration threshold (for example, when the device was dropped).<br>This produces events of the type EVENT. <br>Such events are stateless.<br><br>Events of INSIDE_GEOFENCE and OUTSIDE_GEOFENCE types are generated when the device enters or exits<br>a geofence associated with the device.<br><br>Events of DWELLING_STARTED type are generated when the device has<br>stayed inside an associated geofence for longer than the threshold duration. <br>DWELLING_ENDED type events are generated when dwelling of the device has ended.<br><br>Events of DETENTION_STARTED type are generated when the device has been<br>stationary for longer than the threshold duration, regardless whether the device is inside <br>or outside of any geofence. <br>DETENTION_ENDED type events will be generated when the device starts moving again.<br><br>Events of UNUTILIZED type are generated when the device has been stationary for longer than the<br>threshold duration.<br>UTILIZED type events are generated when the device starts moving again after having been stationary.<br><br>Events of OVERSTOCK, NORMAL_VOLUME and UNDERSTOCK types are generated when the number of assets<br>inside a geofence crosses the `minVolume` and `maxVolume` thresholds of an associated stock rule.<br><br>Events of SHIPMENT_EARLY, SHIPMENT_ON_TIME and SHIPMENT_DELAYED types are generated when a shipment<br>is too early, on time or delayed.<br>|
|» initialState|body|boolean|false|Events with the `initialState` property set as `true` are generated when the rule is <br>evaluated for the first time. It indicates the fact that this is the initial evaluation <br>state, which would serve as a starting point for the subsequent rule evaluations.<br>The rest of the rule events would represent a transition of a device or a shipment or <br>a geofence from one state to another and their `initialState` property will be set to `false`.<br>|
|» ruleId|body|string(uuid)|false|Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|» url|body|string|false|A webhook URL that will receive notifications POST requests.<br>|

## Unregisters from all notifications

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/notifications/v3/registrations \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'x-confirm: true'
```

`DELETE /notifications/v3/registrations`

Deletes all the notification channels. 
This would result in unregistering from all the notifications.

Note that one needs to supply an HTTP header `x-confirm` with the value `true` to force the deletion. 
If the header is not provided, the request will fail.


<h3 id="unregisters-from-all-notifications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-confirm|header|string|true|A safety measure that prevents one from accidentally deleting data.<br><br>To confirm that all entries should be deleted, set the value to `true`.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|x-confirm|true|

```json
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

<h1 id="here-tracking-reports">Reports</h1>

The Reports service provides a way to create and get reports related to event data.

This is a tool for collecting and analyzing historical data of all devices of a project.
The reports are created based on the event data generated by HERE Tracking `rules`.
The supported rule types are:
* dwelling
* detention
* utilization

To be able to create a report, the user must have at least one rule of a supported type created
and associated to a device.

Once a report has been successfully created, the user will get the report ID, which can be used
for various reports queries.

> Note that in the report context a device is also referred to as an 'asset'.


## Starts report creation

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/reports/v4 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "ruleId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /reports/v4`

Starts a report creation.

The request body contains a rule ID, and the report start and end time.
The report will be created based on the event data generated by the rule and devices associated to it.

The supported rule types are:
* dwelling
* detention
* utilization

> Note that both the report start and end timestamps must be earlier than the current time, 
> and no newly ingested data will be automatically added to the report after its creation.

The created report ID will be provided in the response.

The generated report is available for one week, after which it will expire 
and will need to be recreated.
If there is an already existing report matching the request parameters, its `reportId`
will be returned in the response and no new report will be generated.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "end": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "ruleId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "start": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="starts-report-creation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» end|body|string(date-time)|true|End date of the report period. The end date should be greater than the start date.|
|» ruleId|body|string(uuid)|true|Rule ID of a dwelling or detention rule.|
|» start|body|string(date-time)|true|Start date and time of the report period. When getting reports per interval, this timestamp<br>defines the start of the interval day, week or month.<br><br>For example, to make the report week start on Monday midnight 1st March 2021 in timezone UTC+1:00,<br>set the `start` parameter to be `2021-02-28T23:00:00.000Z` (GMT). Now when getting interval reports,<br>the first week would contain data between `2021-02-28T23:00:00.000Z` and `2021-03-07T23:00:00.000Z` (GMT).<br>|

> Example responses

## Gets reports

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/reports/v4/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /reports/v4/{reportId}`

Gets the report creation status and makes queries to fetch the actual reports.
Each report request can have a different set of query parameters.

> Note that in the report context an asset is a device.

Examples
---
To get a report on assets dwelling times in the specified geofence during the report period, 
create a request specifying the following:
* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a dwelling rule
* `measure`: 'duration'
* `groupBy`: 'asset'
* `geofenceId`: geofence ID

To get a report on how many times assets were in detention on average during each week of 
the report period, create a request specifying the following:
* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a detention rule
* `measure`: 'occurrence'
* `method`: 'average'
* `groupBy`: 'asset'
* `interval`: 'week'


<h3 id="gets-reports-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page|
|measure|query|string|false|Defines the report metric to be calculated. <br>The metrics are always calculated over a time period, either over each interval specified <br>by the `interval` parameter (for example, over a week) or over the whole time period of the report.<br><br>* `duration`: duration of the event<br>  * _"The asset dwelled for 45 hours during week 2. It was in detention for 4 hours."_<br>* `occurrence`: total number of the event occurrences<br>  * _"During week 3, the asset was in detention 2 times. During the past month it had 7 individual dwelling periods."_<br>* `day`: the number of days the event lasted<br>  * _"The asset was utilized for 3 days during week 4."_<br>* `asset`: the number of assets that generated the event<br>  * _"On Monday 5 assets were in detention. On Tuesday 16 assets were in detention."_<br>|
|interval|query|string|false|Defines an interval, which can be a day, a week or a month, that will be used to group <br>the report results.<br><br>When the `interval` parameter is provided, the response will be an array of `timestamp`-`value` <br>pairs where the `timestamp` defines the beginning of the interval and the `value` is the specified <br>report metric's value calculated over the interval time.<br>|
|trackingId|query|string|false|Tracking ID.<br>Provide a tracking ID to get a report on a specific asset.<br><br>> Note that in the report context an asset is a device.<br><br>For example, to get a report on how many times the specified asset was in detention during each week,<br>create a request specifying the following:<br>* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a detention rule<br>* `trackingId`: tracking ID<br>* `measure`: 'occurrence'<br>* `interval`: 'week'<br>|
|geofenceId|query|string(uuid)|false|ID of the geofence.<br><br>One can provide a geofence ID in case one wants to get reports on a specific geofence.<br>This parameter can only be used with reports created for a dwelling rule type.<br><br>For example, to get a report on assets' average dwelling time in the specified geofence <br>during each week, create a request specifying the following:<br>* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a dwelling rule<br>* `measure`: 'duration'<br>* `groupBy`: 'asset'<br>* `interval`: 'week'<br>* `method`: 'average'<br>* `geofenceId`: geofence ID<br>|
|groupBy|query|string|false|Defines whether the report metrics, such as cumulative or average, <br>are calculated per asset or per geofence.<br><br>The parameter can have a value 'geofence' only with reports created for a dwelling rule.<br><br>To get a report on how many times on average assets were in detention during each time interval,<br>create a request specifying the following:<br>* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a detention rule<br>* `groupBy`: 'asset'<br>* `method`: 'average'<br>* `measure`: 'occurrence'<br><br>To get a report on how long all assets dwelled inside each geofence during the report period,<br>create a request specifying the following:<br>* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a dwelling rule<br>* `groupBy`: 'geofence'<br>* `measure`: 'duration'<br><br>To get a report on how long each asset dwelled (inside any geofence) during the report period, <br>create a request specifying the following:<br>* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a dwelling rule<br>* `groupBy`: 'asset'<br>* `measure`: 'duration'<br>|
|method|query|string|false|Defines the calculation method. <br>The parameter `method` can only be provided along with `interval`.<br><br>The parameter value can be `percentage` only when `measure` is 'asset'.<br><br>For example, to get a report on percentage of all assets that were in use during each week,<br>create a request specifying the following:<br>* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a utilization rule<br>* `interval`: 'week'<br>* `method`: 'percentage'<br>* `measure`: 'asset'<br><br>When `method` is set to 'cumulative' or 'average' and `measure` is set to 'duration' or 'occurrence',<br>the `groupBy` parameter needs to be provided also. <br>For example, to get a report on how long all assets dwelled in total in the specified geofence during<br>each week, create a request specifying the following:<br>* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a dwelling rule<br>* `geofenceId`: ID of a geofence<br>* `interval`: 'week'<br>* `method`: 'cumulative'<br>* `measure`: 'duration'<br>* `groupBy`: 'asset'<br><br>When `method` is set to 'cumulative' or 'average' and `measure` is set to 'day',<br>the `groupBy` parameter is automatically set to 'asset'. <br>For example, to get a report on how many days on average assets were in use during each month, <br>create a request specifying the following:<br>* `reportId`: ID of a report created for a utilization rule<br>* `interval`: 'month'<br>* `method`: 'average'<br>* `measure`: 'day'<br>* `groupBy`: 'asset'<br>|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines how the items are sorted.<br>* If `interval` is provided, the default is `sort`=`timestamp:asc`<br>* If `interval` is not provided, the default is `sort`=`value:desc`<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|reportId|path|string|true|none|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|measure|duration|
|measure|occurrence|
|measure|day|
|measure|asset|
|interval|day|
|interval|week|
|interval|month|
|groupBy|asset|
|groupBy|geofence|
|method|average|
|method|cumulative|
|method|percentage|

<h1 id="here-tracking-rules">Rules</h1>

The Rules service creates and manages rules. 

Rules generate events and notifications when get triggered by a device behaviour.
The following rule types are supported:
* dwelling
* detention
* utilization
* stock
* online
* shipmentSchedule

After a rule has been created, it needs to be associated to a device to get activated.

This association means that every time a telemetry is received from the device,
it will be evaluated against the rule condition.
As soon as the evaluation changes (for example, from true to false), an event will be recorded.

## Creates a rule

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rules/v4 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "threshold": {
      "durationS": 0
    },
    "type": "utilization"
  }'
```

`POST /rules/v4`

Creates a rule of the specified rule `type` and with the defined `threshold`.
After the rule has been created, it needs to be associated to a device to get activated.

Detention rule
---
For a rule of the `detention` type the threshold is defined as a duration in seconds.
A `DETENTION_STARTED` event gets triggered when the device has remained
stationary for longer than the threshold duration.
A `DETENTION_ENDED` event will be generated when the device starts moving again.

Utilization rule
---
For a rule of the `utilization` type the threshold is defined as a duration in seconds.
An `UNUTILIZED` event will
be generated when the device has been stationary for longer than the threshold duration, 
and `UTILIZED` event gets triggered when the device starts moving again after having been stationary.

Dwelling rule
---
For a rule of the `dwelling` type the threshold is defined as a duration in seconds.
A `DWELLING_STARTED` event gets triggered when a dwelling time of the device
inside any device-associated geofence exceeds the threshold duration.
When the device exits the geofence, a `DWELLING_ENDED` event will be generated.

Online rule
---
For a rule of the `online` type there is no threshold defined.
A `TRUE_TO_FALSE` event gets triggered when the
device is late for the planned ingestion schedule by more than 5 minutes.
A `FALSE_TO_TRUE` event is generated when the device starts ingesting again after having been offline.
The planned ingestion schedule needs to be configured in the device `desired shadow`
(the `desired.system.rate.sendMs` property).

Stock rule
---
For a rule of the `stock` type the threshold is defined as `minVolume` and/or `maxVolume` values.
When creating a stock rule, also a geofence ID needs to be specified.
When the number of devices inside the specified geofence exceeds `maxVolume`, an `OVERSTOCK`
event will be generated. Similarly, when the number of devices inside the specified geofence
gets below `minVolume`, an `UNDERSTOCK` event will be generated. When the number of
devices inside the specified geofence is between `minVolume` and `maxVolume`, a `NORMAL_VOLUME`
event will be generated. Note that the stock rule only gets triggered for devices that are associated
to the specified geofence.

Shipment schedule rule
---
For a rule of the `shipmentSchedule` type there are `before` and `after` deviation time thresholds 
from the planned shipment ETD/ETA.
A `SHIPMENT_EARLY` event gets triggered when the shipment is ahead
of schedule by the number of `before` seconds.
A `SHIPMENT_DELAYED` event gets triggered when the shipment is behind
schedule by the number of `after` seconds.
A `SHIPMENT_ON_TIME` event gets triggered when the shipment is on time.

When a rule has been successfully created, the response body will contain the created rule ID.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "threshold": {
    "durationS": 0
  },
  "type": "utilization"
}
```

## Deletes all rules

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rules/v4 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'x-confirm: true'
```

`DELETE /rules/v4`

Deletes all rules of the project.

Note that one needs to supply an HTTP header `x-confirm` with the value `true` to force the deletion.
If the header is not provided, the request will fail.


<h3 id="deletes-all-rules-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|

## Updates a single rule

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/rules/v4/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "threshold": {
      "durationS": 0
    },
    "type": "utilization"
  }'
```

`PUT /rules/v4/{ruleId}`

Updates the name, description and threshold of the rule `ruleId`. 
The rule type cannot be updated.
If some of the these properties are not provided in the request body, their values
will be set to null.

If the rule has been updated successfully, the response will contain the updated rule details.

```json

  "name": "string",

}
```

<h1 id="here-tracking-sensors">Sensors</h1>

The Sensors service creates and manages sensor rules. 

The sensor rules generate events and notifications when get triggered by a 
reported device sensor reading.

The following sensor rule types are supported:
* battery
* humidity
* pressure
* temperature
* acceleration
* attach
* tamper

After a sensor rule has been created, it needs to be associated to a device to get activated.

This association means that every time a sensor update is received from the device as a part 
of its ingestion telemetry, it will be evaluated against the sensor rule condition.
As soon as the evaluation changes (for example, from true to false), an event will be recorded.

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sensors/v3 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## Creates a sensor rule

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sensors/v3 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "range": {
      "begin": 0,
      "end": 0
    },
    "type": "battery"
  }'
```

`POST /sensors/v3`

Creates a sensor rule of the specified rule type.
After the sensor rule has been created, it needs to be associated to a device to get activated.

For a sensor rule of the battery, humidity, pressure and temperature type, a `range` parameter needs 
to be specified, defining both upper and lower thresholds for the sensor readings. 
When the device ingests data, the reported sensor reading is compared to the defined range 
and in case in or out of range transition has taken place, an event gets triggered.

For a sensor rule of the acceleration type, a `threshold` parameter needs 
to be specified, defining the acceleration threshold value.
Every time the device reports its accelerometer sensor reading being above the threshold, 
an event gets triggered.

For a sensor rule of the attach and tamper types, no additional parameters
need to be specified.
The attach sensor detects whether the device is attached to some object (for example to an 
asset).
The tamper sensor detects whether the device cover is open or closed. When the cover is open,
the device is considered to be tampered with.
Every time the device reports getting attached, detached, tampered with or left with the 
cover closed (that is, not tampered with), an event gets triggered.

When a sensor rule has been successfully created, the response body will contain the created rule ID.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "range": {
    "begin": 0,
    "end": 0
  },
  "type": "battery"
}
```

## Deletes all sensor rules

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sensors/v3 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'x-confirm: true'
```

`DELETE /sensors/v3`

Deletes all sensor rules of a project.

Note that one needs to supply an HTTP header `x-confirm` with the value `true` to force the deletion. 
If the header is not provided, the request will fail.

|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

<h1 id="here-tracking-shadows">Shadows</h1>

The Shadows service provides an effective way to manage configurations 
for devices that are only intermittently online.

The device shadow contains `reported` and `desired` state objects of a device, 
referred to as `reported` and `desired` shadows.

The `desired` shadow contains configuration settings that the device should use and possibly also
some optional custom settings. 
The device receives the `desired` shadow from HERE Tracking as a response to the ingestion request.

The `reported` shadow contains the most recent position, sensor readings and settings that the
device has sent. The reported shadow may also contain additional properties generated by HERE 
Tracking based on the device-ingested telemetry. Such properties are stored in the `system.computed` 
property.

In case the most recent telemetry did not contain all the possible
fields, the last known information will remain in the shadow. This means that one can
see, for example, the last reported temperature or tracker firmware information in the reported shadow,
even if the device did not send that information in the latest telemetry.

> **IMPORTANT**
> Devices should not communicate directly with this service, but should instead send the telemetry to
> the ingestion endpoint, which updates the `reported` shadow and returns the `desired` shadow.
> Applications should only write to the `desired` shadow and only read from the 
> `reported` shadow.


## Gets a batch of device shadows

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shadows/v2/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    "HERE-6da0f871-b4eb-4800-90e6-4bae86a788d6",
    "HERE-b0146d7b-2e46-4cee-bc71-6da03ba2da85"
  ]'
```

`POST /shadows/v2/batch`

Gets device shadows for multiple devices. One can get shadows for a
maximum of 100 devices per request.

In case `after` parameter is provided, only the device
shadows that were modified on or after the specified timestamp
will be retrieved.


> Body parameter

```json
[
  "HERE-6da0f871-b4eb-4800-90e6-4bae86a788d6",
  "HERE-b0146d7b-2e46-4cee-bc71-6da03ba2da85"
]
```

<h3 id="gets-a-batch-of-device-shadows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|after|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 0 to the current time.<br>|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|body|body|[string]|false|none|

```bash
curl https://example.com/shadows/v2/health \

```

```json
}
```

## Gets a device shadow

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shadows/v2/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /shadows/v2/{trackingId}`

Gets the `trackingId` device shadow that contains both `reported` and `desired` shadows.

If a `shipmentId` is used instead of a `trackingId`, it will return a
shadow of the device that was most recently active for the shipment. If the shipment
is still pending or it has been cancelled or completed, an empty shadow will be returned.


<h3 id="gets-a-device-shadow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "desired": {
    "payload": {
      "color": "red",
      "velocity": 100
    }
  },
  "reported": {
    "payload": {
      "color": "blue",
      "velocity": 100
    },
    "position": {
      "alt": 97,
      "lat": 52.5,
      "lng": 13.4
    }
  },
  "timestamp": 1461065261010
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 401,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 401306
  },
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The provided credentials are not valid."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 403,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 403306
  },
  "error": "Forbidden",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The account does not have the correct privileges."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
[
  {
    "code": 401,
    "details": {
      "hereErrorCode": 401306
    },
    "error": "Unauthorized",
    "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee",
    "message": "Invalid Authorization, the request lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource."
  }
]
```

<h3 id="gets-a-device-shadow-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful<br><br>The device shadow was successfully retrieved.<br>|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request<br><br>The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range.<br><br>If available, further error details are provided in the response body.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized<br><br>The request did not provide correct authentication details<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden<br><br>The account does not have the correct privileges<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found. No shadow exists for the requested trackingId.|Inline|

## Updates a device shadow

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shadows/v2/string \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'content-length: 0' \
  -d '{
    "desired": {
      "payload": {},
      "system": {
        "detectOutliers": true,
        "disableTracking": {
          "periods": [
            {
              "begin": 2,
              "end": 2
            }
          ],
          "position": "all",
          "sensors": "all"
        },
        "rate": {
          "distanceM": 0,
          "sampleMs": 0,
          "sendMs": 0
        },
        "sensorLoggingConfigurations": [
          {
            "samplingFrequency": 1,
            "type": "acceleration"
          }
        ],
        "sensorLoggingEnabled": true,
        "syncGeofences": true,
        "wlanConfigurations": [
          {
            "password": "stringst",
            "securityMode": "none",
            "ssid": "string",
            "ssidIsHidden": true
          }
        ],
        "wlanConnectivityEnabled": true
      }
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /shadows/v2/{trackingId}`

Updates the `trackingId` device desired shadow.

The device shadow consists of `reported` and `desired` shadows. 
Only the `desired` shadow can be updated via this endpoint.
The `reported` shadow is updated automatically when the device sends telemetry to the ingestion endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "desired": {
    "payload": {},
    "system": {
      "detectOutliers": true,
      "disableTracking": {
        "periods": [
          {
            "begin": 2,
            "end": 2
          }
        ],
        "position": "all",
        "sensors": "all"
      },
      "rate": {
        "distanceM": 0,
        "sampleMs": 0,
        "sendMs": 0
      },
      "sensorLoggingConfigurations": [
        {
          "samplingFrequency": 1,
          "type": "acceleration"
        }
      ],
      "sensorLoggingEnabled": true,
      "syncGeofences": true,
      "wlanConfigurations": [
        {
          "password": "stringst",
          "securityMode": "none",
          "ssid": "string",
          "ssidIsHidden": true
        }
      ],
      "wlanConnectivityEnabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="updates-a-device-shadow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|content-length|header|number|true|The size of the shadow in bytes. The size is validated against the<br>maximum limit of 1000 bytes.<br>|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» desired|body|object|true|The desired shadow of the device.<br>|
|» » payload|body|object|false|A free format JSON object.<br>The maximum size is 1000B.<br>|
|» » system|body|object|false|Contains values for the device configuration. HERE Tracking uses these values<br>for various application flows.<br>|
|» » » detectOutliers|body|boolean|false|A boolean value that sets outlier detection on or off|
|» » » disableTracking|body|object|false|Tracking can be disabled and enabled by defining disableTracking object.<br>In order to disable tracking, one must at least provide the begin time of the disabling<br>period and define either position or sensor properties one wants to disable. One can also<br>disable both position and sensors at the same time. By default tracking is enabled.<br>|
|» » » » periods|body|[object]|false|Define begin and end of the disabling period. All trace points with timestamp that falls between begin and end times will be disabled according to the settings defined in the position and sensors properties.<br>|
|» » » » » begin|body|integer|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC<br><br>Begin time of the tracking disabling period.<br><br>Begin must be smaller than end. Begin must be greater or equal to current time.<br>Begin can be set without end. If there exists already end time which is earlier<br>than given new begin time, the existing end time will be deleted.<br>|
|» » » » » end|body|integer|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC<br><br>End time of the tracking disabling period.<br><br>End must be greater than begin. End must be greater or equal to current time.<br>End can be set without begin if begin is already set.<br>|
|» » » » position|body|string \| [string]|false|Define position methods to be disabled|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|All positioning data the device sends will be removed before further processing. No geofence and location events will be generated<br>|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|By setting the position property empty string, all positioning data will be re-enabled during the disabling period.<br>|
|» » » » sensors|body|string \| [string]|false|Define sensors to be disabled|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|All sensor data the device sends will be removed before further processing. No sensor events will be generated.<br>|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|[string]|false|none|
|» » » » » *oneOf*|body|string|false|By setting the sensors property empty string, all sensors data will be re-enabled during the disabling period.<br>|
|» » » rate|body|object|false|This can be used to specify the rates at which the device performs certain tasks.|
|» » » » distanceM|body|number|false|Send an update if the device has moved farther than the specified distance in meters|
|» » » » sampleMs|body|number|false|The rate at which to sample signals in milliseconds|
|» » » » sendMs|body|number|false|The rate at which to send sample results in milliseconds|
|» » » sensorLoggingConfigurations|body|[object]|false|An array of objects that holds sensor logging configurations|
|» » » » samplingFrequency|body|number|false|Sampling frequrency of single sensor loggin configuration (in milliseconds)|
|» » » » type|body|string|true|Type of single sensor logging configuration|
|» » » sensorLoggingEnabled|body|boolean|false|Flag that sets sensor logging on or off|
|» » » syncGeofences|body|boolean|false|A boolean value that sets efficient geofencing on or off|
|» » » wlanConfigurations|body|[object]|false|An array of objects that holds wlan configurations|
|» » » » password|body|string|false|WLAN password. Please note that the password is stored to the device unencrypted. Do not use secure private networks, such as Intranet, for tracker WLAN connectivity. Password is required if security mode is other then 'none'.|
|» » » » securityMode|body|string|true|Selected security mode|
|» » » » ssid|body|string|true|Name given to a WLAN that is used by the client to access a WLAN network. Please note that the SSID is stored to the device unencrypted. Do not use secure private networks, such as Intranet, for tracker WLAN connectivity.|
|» » » » ssidIsHidden|body|boolean|false|Flag that informs if SSID is hidden|
|» » » wlanConnectivityEnabled|body|boolean|false|A boolean value that sets wlan connectivity on or off|

## Clears a device shadow

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shadows/v2/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /shadows/v2/{trackingId}`

Deletes the device shadow of the `trackingId` device.

By default, all the values of the `desired` and `reported` shadow objects will be cleared, leaving them empty.

If either `desired` or `reported` query parameter is set to `false`, that part of the shadow remains as it is.


<h3 id="clears-a-device-shadow-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|desired|query|boolean|false|If `true`, all the values of the `desired` shadow will be cleared|
|reported|query|boolean|false|If `true`, all the values of the `reported` shadow will be cleared|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 401,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 401306
  },
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The provided credentials are not valid."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 403,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 403306
  },
  "error": "Forbidden",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The account does not have the correct privileges."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
[
  {
    "code": 401,
    "details": {
      "hereErrorCode": 401306
    },
    "error": "Unauthorized",
    "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee",
    "message": "Invalid Authorization, the request lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource."
  }
]
```

<h3 id="clears-a-device-shadow-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Successful (no content)|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request<br><br>The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range.<br><br>If available, further error details are provided in the response body.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized<br><br>The request did not provide correct authentication details<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden<br><br>The account does not have the correct privileges<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not found. No shadow exists for the requested trackingId.|Inline|

## Gets reported or desired state object of a device

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shadows/v2/string/desired \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /shadows/v2/{trackingId}/{state}`

Gets the `reported` or `desired` state object of the device `trackingId`, that is the `reported` or `desired` device shadow.


<h3 id="gets-reported-or-desired-state-object-of-a-device-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|state|path|string|true|Desired or reported state object of a device to query.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|desired|
|state|reported|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "position": {
    "accuracy": "18",
    "alt": "105",
    "altaccuracy": "15",
    "lat": "52.5308544",
    "lng": "13.38480101"
  }
}
```

```json
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

```json
  },
```

```json
  },
```

## Gets a value of a shadow property

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shadows/v2/string/desired/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /shadows/v2/{trackingId}/{state}/{selector}`

Gets a value of a single property of either `desired` or `reported` state objects of a device.
One can use JSON selectors to specify the target property or reference it by name.
In case the property contains an object, the entire object will be returned in the response.

The JSON selector can be nested like this: `payload/time/minutes`


<h3 id="gets-a-value-of-a-shadow-property-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|state|path|string|true|Desired or reported state object of a device to query.|
|selector|path|string|true|A JSON selector that specifies the property.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|state|desired|
|state|reported|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "accuracy": "18",
  "alt": "105",
  "altaccuracy": "15",
  "lat": "52.5308544",
  "lng": "13.38480101"
}
```

```json
}
```

## Gets all shadows

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shadows/v4 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /shadows/v4`

Gets all device shadows of a project.


<h3 id="gets-all-shadows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page|
|after|query|string(date-time)|false|If provided returns the shadows for which `reported.timestamp` is greater than given `after` parameter.|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines how the items are sorted.<br>The default sort is `sort=trackingId:asc`<br>|
|bbox|query|[number]|false|Limit search to shadows, whose position intersects the given bounding box.<br>The `bbox` array consist of latitude and longitude of Northwest and Southeast corners.<br>|

|400|Bad Request|Bad request<br><br>The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range.<br><br>If available, further error details are provided in the response body.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized<br><br>The request did not provide correct authentication details<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden<br><br>The account does not have the correct privileges<br>|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found<br><br>The specified resource was not found<br>|Inline|

<h3 id="gets-all-shadows-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|count|integer|true|none|Number of items returned in the response|
|items|[object]|true|none|none|

<h1 id="here-tracking-shipment-reports">Shipment Reports</h1>

Service for generating and viewing shipment reports.

This is an alpha version of the Shipment Reports API and can still be changed in future
releases.

A shipment report consists of different metrics calculated on shipments which have been completed successfully.

Punctuality at origin or at destination measures how accurate the estimated
departure or arrival was. Dwelling at location measures how much time was spent at locations.

The metrics are split into two categories. The first category consists of metrics which are calculated
over all shipments of a shipment plan. The second category consists of metrics which are calculated on
individual shipments of a shipment plan.
For example, the `location` metrics belongs to the first category.
Statistical values, such as `average`, are produced for metrics of the first category only.


## Starts shipment report generation

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipment-reports/v4 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "endedAfter": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "endedBefore": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "shipmentPlanIds": [
      "string"
    ],
    "startedAfter": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "startedBefore": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

`POST /shipment-reports/v4`

This endpoint starts the shipment report generation. One can specify which shipments to include
in the shipments report by using the filters in the request body. The response contains the generated
shipment report ID `shipmentReportId`.

After the shipment report generation has been requested, the status of the shipment report generation
can be checked by using the `/shipment-reports/v4/{shipmentReportId}/status` endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "endedAfter": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "endedBefore": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "shipmentPlanIds": [
    "string"
  ],
  "startedAfter": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "startedBefore": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<h3 id="starts-shipment-report-generation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» endedAfter|body|string(date-time)|false|Include successfully completed shipments of each shipment plan into the shipment report generation<br>which ended after the provided date.<br>|
|» endedBefore|body|string(date-time)|false|Include successfully completed shipments of each shipment plan into the shipment report generation<br>which ended before the provided date.<br>|
|» shipmentPlanIds|body|[string]|false|Provide array of shipment plan ids to include into the shipment report. If just a single shipment plan id is<br>given, then the shipment report will include only metrics and shipments for the given shipment plan. If none<br>is given, then the shipment report will include all shipment plans.<br>|
|» startedAfter|body|string(date-time)|false|Include successfully completed shipments of each shipment plan into the shipment report generation<br>which started after the provided date.<br>|
|» startedBefore|body|string(date-time)|false|Include successfully completed shipments of each shipment plan into the shipment report generation<br>which started before the provided date.<br>|

```json
{
  "shipmentReportId": "string"
}
```
