<h1 id="here-tracking-shipments">Shipments</h1>

The Shipments service manages shipments and shipment plans.

This is an Alpha version of the Shipments API and can still be changed in future releases.

A shipment describes a structure of a multimodal logistics journey. Shipments are useful when
the lifetime of an asset one is tracking spans across multiple devices.

A shipment consists of segments that span from a location to another. The segments and their
origins and destinations must form a continuous chain of locations, that is the origin of a segment
must match the destination of a previous segment. Each segment of the shipment may be assigned a
`trackingId` that can vary between segments. Devices assigned to a shipment generate traces
and events for the entire shipment.

The `shipmentId` of a shipment can be used in similar fashion as a `trackingId` in selected
APIs. For example, one can query for shipment ***traces*** and ***events*** and associate ***aliases*** and
***metadata*** to a shipment.

Each shipment has one of the following statuses:
* ***pending***: The shipment has not yet started.
* ***ongoing***: The shipment has started and it has one segment ongoing.
* ***completed***: The shipment has ended and all of its segments are completed.
* ***cancelled***: The shipment has ended and it has one or more cancelled segments.

HERE Tracking progresses the shipment automatically if each segment has been assigned a
`trackingId` and the origin and destination locations contain a `geofenceId`. Each segment is
started upon exiting the origin location of the segment and completed upon entering the
destination location of the segment. If the origin and the destination of a segment share the
same location (that is, dwelling in a single location), the segment will automatically be started after the
previous segment was completed. If a segment does not have a device assigned, the user must
start and complete the segment manually.

A new shipment should be instantiated for each separate logistical journey. However, if the
structure of the shipment is recurring, a shipment plan can be defined. A shipment plan can
be used to define a generic skeleton for a logistical journey. For example, certain types
of assets often need to be shipped over a typical sequence of locations.
A user can create a shipment plan defining the segments, and new shipments can be instantiated from the plan.
This allows recycling of components for similar shipments and reduces time and effort for
creating new shipment instances.

Shipments can also be created, managed and visualized via the [Shipment Tracking web](https://shipment.tracking.here.com).

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page|
|status|query|string|false|Filter the results by shipment status|
|startedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only shipments that started before the specified timestamp|
|startedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only shipments that started after the specified timestamp|
|endedBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only shipments that ended before the specified timestamp|
|endedAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only shipments that ended after the specified timestamp|
|name|query|string|false|Filter shipments by name. Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|shipmentPlanId|query|string|false|Return only shipments that have been instantiated from the specified `shipmentPlanId`|
|shipmentId|query|string|false|Filter shipments by `shipmentId`<br>Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|isSubShipment|query|boolean|false|Returns only shipments marked as subShipments|
|createdBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only shipments that have been created before specified timestamp|
|createdAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only shipments that have been created after specified timestamp|
|sort|query|string \| [string]|false|A paramater to specify field to sort by and order.<br>The following format can be used:<br>'name:asc' sort by name in ascending order,<br>'shipmentId:desc' sort by shipmentId in descending order.<br>Allowed fields to sort by:<br>shipmentId, name, status, startedAt, createdAt, endedAt, providedEtd,<br>providedEta, calculatedEtd.<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

|status|completed|
|status|cancelled|

## Creates a shipment

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipments/v4 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoStart": true,
    "description": "A shipment consisting of four segments",
    "name": "From Portugal to Panama",
    "ruleIds": [
      "712dde2c-20e6-4903-82f1-0beb0dd9e4bd",
      "6d1da24b-5187-42ab-9eb5-1e43c61b6bae"
    ],
    "segments": [
      {
        "description": "From factory to port",
        "destination": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
        "name": "Truck transport",
        "origin": "LOC-54531862-f87a-4b70-99a4-0e8224a56be4",
        "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
        "transportMode": "truck"
      },
      {
        "description": "From port to another port",
        "destination": "LOC-a2dc2c70-cc3e-4fa5-ac77-4c63558e7f97",
        "name": "Marine transport",
        "origin": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
        "trackingId": "VRTR-8b9fd950-ce19-4aaf-98d5-840a76652658",
        "transportMode": "sea"
      },
      {
        "description": "From port to storage",
        "destination": "LOC-733deb91-efa3-41b6-9003-92845866b511",
        "name": "Truck transport",
        "origin": "LOC-a2dc2c70-cc3e-4fa5-ac77-4c63558e7f97",
        "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
        "transportMode": "truck"
      }
    ],
    "subShipment": false
  }'
```

`POST /shipments/v4`

Creates a new shipment. A shipment consists of segments each representing a part of the
logistics journey. A segment spans from a location to another and each segment may be
assigned a different tracking device.

The segments of the shipment must form a continuous chain of locations, that is the origin of a
segment must match the destination of a previous segment.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoStart": true,
  "description": "A shipment consisting of four segments",
  "name": "From Portugal to Panama",
  "ruleIds": [
    "712dde2c-20e6-4903-82f1-0beb0dd9e4bd",
    "6d1da24b-5187-42ab-9eb5-1e43c61b6bae"
  ],
  "segments": [
    {
      "description": "From factory to port",
      "destination": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
      "name": "Truck transport",
      "origin": "LOC-54531862-f87a-4b70-99a4-0e8224a56be4",
      "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
      "transportMode": "truck"
    },
    {
      "description": "From port to another port",
      "destination": "LOC-a2dc2c70-cc3e-4fa5-ac77-4c63558e7f97",
      "name": "Marine transport",
      "origin": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
      "trackingId": "VRTR-8b9fd950-ce19-4aaf-98d5-840a76652658",
      "transportMode": "sea"
    },
    {
      "description": "From port to storage",
      "destination": "LOC-733deb91-efa3-41b6-9003-92845866b511",
      "name": "Truck transport",
      "origin": "LOC-a2dc2c70-cc3e-4fa5-ac77-4c63558e7f97",
      "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
      "transportMode": "truck"
    }
  ],
  "subShipment": false
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-shipment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|Body for creating a shipment|
|» autoStart|body|boolean|false|A boolean parameter defining whether the shipment starts upon exiting the first origin<br>location.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the shipment|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the shipment|
|» providedEta|body|string(date-time)|false|ETA for the shipment|
|» providedEtd|body|string(date-time)|false|ETD for the shipment|
|» ruleIds|body|[string(uuid)]|false|Array of `ruleId`s to associate with the shipment|
|» segments|body|[object]|true|Array of objects each defining the origin and destination of the segment|
|» » description|body|string|false|Description of the segment|
|» » destination|body|string|true|Destination location of this segment|
|» » name|body|string|false|Name of the segment|
|» » origin|body|string|true|Origin location of this segment|
|» » providedEta|body|string(date-time)|false|ETA for the segment|
|» » providedEtd|body|string(date-time)|false|ETD for the segment|
|» » trackingId|body|string|false|ID of the tracking device that produces data for this segment|
|» » transportMode|body|string|true|Transport mode of the segment|
|» subShipment|body|boolean|false|Flag telling if shipment is a subShipment.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|Create shipment from an existing shipment plan|
|» shipmentDeparture|body|string(date-time)|false|ETD of the shipment instance. Used to calculate the ETDs and ETAs of all the segments based on the segment durations defined in the plan.|
|» shipmentPlanId|body|string|true|Shipment plan ID|

## Deletes all shipments

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipments/v4 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'x-confirm: true'
```

`DELETE /shipments/v4`

Deletes all the shipments of the project.

Note that one needs to supply an HTTP header `x-confirm` with the value `true` to force the deletion.
If the header is not provided, the request will fail.


<h3 id="deletes-all-shipments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-confirm|header|string|true|A safety measure that prevents one from accidentally deleting data.<br><br>To confirm that all entries should be deleted, set the value to `true`.<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|x-confirm|true|

> Example responses

```json
  "code": 400,

    "hereErrorCode": 400306

  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

## Lists all shipment plans

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipments/v4/plans \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /shipments/v4/plans`

Gets all shipment plans of the project.


<h3 id="lists-all-shipment-plans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page|
|name|query|string|false|Filter shipments by name. Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|shipmentPlanId|query|string|false|Return only shipment plans that have been instantiated from the specified `shipmentPlanId`<br>Matching is case-insensitive.<br>The following wildcards can be used:<br>'*' matches any number of any characters,<br>'?' matches any single character.<br>|
|locationId|query|string|false|Return only shipments that have been instantiated from the specified `locationId`<br>|
|createdBefore|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only shipments that have been created before specified timestamp|
|createdAfter|query|string(date-time)|false|Return only shipments that have been created after specified timestamp|
|isSubShipment|query|boolean|false|Returns only shipments marked as subShipments|
|sort|query|string \| [string]|false|A paramater to specify field to sort by and order.<br>Allowed fields to sort by: shipmentPlanId, name, createdAt<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

## Creates a shipment plan

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipments/v4/plans \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoStart": true,
    "description": "A shipment consisting of four segments",
    "name": "From Portugal to Panama",
    "segments": [
      {
        "description": "From factory to port",
        "destination": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
        "durationS": 10800,
        "name": "Truck transport",
        "origin": "LOC-54531862-f87a-4b70-99a4-0e8224a56be4",
        "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
        "transportMode": "truck"
      },
      {
        "description": "From port to another port",
        "destination": "LOC-a2dc2c70-cc3e-4fa5-ac77-4c63558e7f97",
        "durationS": 129600,
        "name": "Marine transport",
        "origin": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
        "trackingId": "VRTR-8b9fd950-ce19-4aaf-98d5-840a76652658",
        "transportMode": "sea"
      },
      {
        "description": "From port to storage",
        "destination": "LOC-733deb91-efa3-41b6-9003-92845866b511",
        "durationS": 7200,
        "name": "Truck transport",
        "origin": "LOC-a2dc2c70-cc3e-4fa5-ac77-4c63558e7f97",
        "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
        "transportMode": "truck"
      }
    ],
    "subShipment": false
  }'
```

`POST /shipments/v4/plans`

Creates a new shipment plan. A shipment plan is a structure that holds information about a
recurring shipment. Like a shipment, a shipment plan also consists of segments each
representing a part of the logistics journey. A segment spans from a location to another and
each segment may be assigned a different tracking device. The segments of the shipment must form a
continuous chain of locations, that is the origin of a segment must match the destination of a
previous segment.

In addition to shipments, a predefined duration can be assigned to each segment in the plan.
This information will be used to calculate the Estimated Time of Departure (ETD) and
Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) when instantiating a shipment from a shipment plan.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoStart": true,
  "description": "A shipment consisting of four segments",
  "name": "From Portugal to Panama",
  "segments": [
    {
      "description": "From factory to port",
      "destination": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
      "durationS": 10800,
      "name": "Truck transport",
      "origin": "LOC-54531862-f87a-4b70-99a4-0e8224a56be4",
      "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
      "transportMode": "truck"
    },
    {
      "description": "From port to another port",
      "destination": "LOC-a2dc2c70-cc3e-4fa5-ac77-4c63558e7f97",
      "durationS": 129600,
      "name": "Marine transport",
      "origin": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
      "trackingId": "VRTR-8b9fd950-ce19-4aaf-98d5-840a76652658",
      "transportMode": "sea"
    },
    {
      "description": "From port to storage",
      "destination": "LOC-733deb91-efa3-41b6-9003-92845866b511",
      "durationS": 7200,
      "name": "Truck transport",
      "origin": "LOC-a2dc2c70-cc3e-4fa5-ac77-4c63558e7f97",
      "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
      "transportMode": "truck"
    }
  ],
  "subShipment": false
}
```

<h3 id="creates-a-shipment-plan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» autoStart|body|boolean|false|A boolean parameter defining whether the shipment starts upon exiting the first origin<br>location.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the shipment|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the shipment|
|» ruleIds|body|[string(uuid)]|false|Array of `ruleId`s to associate with the shipment|
|» segments|body|[object]|true|Array of objects each defining the origin and destination of the segment|
|» » description|body|string|false|Description of the segment|
|» » destination|body|string|true|Destination location of this segment|
|» » durationS|body|integer|false|Segment duration in seconds.|
|» » name|body|string|false|Name of the segment|
|» » origin|body|string|true|Origin location of this segment|
|» » trackingId|body|string|false|ID of the tracking device that produces data for this segment|
|» » transportMode|body|string|true|Transport mode of the segment|
|» subShipment|body|boolean|false|Flag telling if shipment is a subShipment.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» options|body|object|false|Optional parameters for plan creation|
|» » calculateDurationsFrom|body|string|false|If defined, the durations of the segments in the plan will be based on the durations of the segments of the provided shipment|
|» » copyTrackingIds|body|boolean|false|If set to `true`, trackingIds in the segments of the provided shipment are copied to the plan|
|» shipmentId|body|string|true|Shipment ID|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|

|» » transportMode|truck|
|» » transportMode|sea|
|» » transportMode|air|

|» » calculateDurationsFrom|providedEstimate|
|» » calculateDurationsFrom|calculatedEstimate|

## Deletes all shipment plans

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipments/v4/plans \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'x-confirm: true'
```

`DELETE /shipments/v4/plans`

Deletes all shipment plans of the project. Any shipments instantiated from the plans will
persist, but the references to the parent plans will be removed.

Note that one needs to supply an HTTP header `x-confirm` with the value `true` to force the deletion.
If the header is not provided, the request will fail.


<h3 id="deletes-all-shipment-plans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-confirm|header|string|true|A safety measure that prevents one from accidentally deleting data.<br><br>To confirm that all entries should be deleted, set the value to `true`.<br>|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|x-confirm|true|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json

  "code": 401,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 401306
  },
  "error": "Unauthorized",

  "message": "The provided credentials are not valid."
```

## Updates a shipment plan details

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipments/v4/plans/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoStart": true,
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "ruleIds": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "subShipment": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /shipments/v4/plans/{shipmentPlanId}`

Updates details of a shipment plan identified by the `shipmentPlanId`.
This is a partial update, meaning that only the provided
fields will be updated. If `ruleIds` field is specified, it will replace
the existing rules currently associated with the shipment plan.

***Note***:
`segments` cannot be edited through this API. Changing the order of the segments in a plan
would cause shipments created from earlier versions of the plan diverge from a shipment
instantiated from the new plan with different segment structure. Individual segments can
still be updated via the `shipments/v4/plans/{shipmentPlanId}/{segmentPlanId}` endpoint.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoStart": true,
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "ruleIds": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "subShipment": true
}
```

<h3 id="updates-a-shipment-plan-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|shipmentPlanId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» autoStart|body|boolean|false|A boolean parameter defining whether the shipment starts upon exiting the first origin<br>location.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the shipment|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the shipment|
|» ruleIds|body|[string(uuid)]|false|Array of `ruleId`s to associate with the shipment|
|» subShipment|body|boolean|false|Flag telling if shipment is a subShipment.|

## Updates a shipment details

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipments/v4/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "autoStart": true,
    "description": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "providedEta": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "providedEtd": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "ruleIds": [
      "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
    ],
    "segments": [
      {
        "description": "From factory to port",
        "destination": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
        "name": "Truck transport",
        "origin": "LOC-54531862-f87a-4b70-99a4-0e8224a56be4",
        "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
        "transportMode": "truck"
      }
    ],
    "status": "pending",
    "subShipment": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /shipments/v4/{shipmentId}`

Updates details of a shipment identified by the `shipmentId`.
This is a partial update, meaning that only the provided fields will be updated,
except when updating segments, the whole segments will be replaced fully.

Changing the status of the shipment affects the statuses of the segments. The following
status changes are allowed:
* `pending` → `ongoing`
  * changes the status of the first segment to `ongoing`
* `pending` → `cancelled`
  * changes the status of all segments to `cancelled`
* `ongoing` → `cancelled`
  * cancels the current `ongoing` segment and all the succeeding segments
* `ongoing` → `completed`
  * completes the current `ongoing` segment and cancels all the succeeding segments

***Note***:
`segments` and `autoStart` can be updated via this API call only if the shipment is in
`pending` state.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "autoStart": true,
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "providedEta": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "providedEtd": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "ruleIds": [
    "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  ],
  "segments": [
    {
      "description": "From factory to port",
      "destination": "LOC-7b6b15cc-2307-4875-9f66-99deb5227e92",
      "name": "Truck transport",
      "origin": "LOC-54531862-f87a-4b70-99a4-0e8224a56be4",
      "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
      "transportMode": "truck"
    }
  ],
  "status": "pending",
  "subShipment": true
}
```

<h3 id="updates-a-shipment-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|shipmentId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» autoStart|body|boolean|false|A boolean parameter defining whether the shipment starts upon exiting the first origin<br>location.<br>|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the shipment|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the shipment|
|» providedEta|body|string(date-time)|false|ETA for the shipment|
|» providedEtd|body|string(date-time)|false|ETD for the shipment|

|» segments|body|[object]|false|Array of objects each defining the origin and destination of the segment|
|» » description|body|string|false|Description of the segment|
|» » destination|body|string|true|Destination location of this segment|
|» » name|body|string|false|Name of the segment|
|» » origin|body|string|true|Origin location of this segment|

|» » trackingId|body|string|false|ID of the tracking device that produces data for this segment|

## Updates a segment details

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shipments/v4/string/string \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "From factory to port",
    "name": "Truck transport",
    "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
    "transportMode": "truck"
  }'
```

`PATCH /shipments/v4/{shipmentId}/{segmentId}`

Updates details of a segment identified by the `segmentId`.

This is a partial update, meaning that only the provided fields
will be updated.

Changing the status of a segment affects the statuses of other segments in the shipment. The
following status changes are allowed:
* `pending` → `ongoing`
  * changes previous `pending` segments to `cancelled`
  * changes previous `ongoing` segment to `completed` (only for the immediate predecessor of
    this segment)
  * changes previous `ongoing` segment to `cancelled` (for segments that are not immediate
    predecessors of this segment)
  * previous segments in `cancelled` or `completed` states are not affected
* `pending` || `ongoing` → `cancelled`
  * no changes for other segments
* `ongoing` → `completed`
  * next segment with status `pending` is changed to `ongoing`

***Note***:
`trackingId` can be updated through this API call only if the segment is in `pending` state.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "From factory to port",
  "name": "Truck transport",
  "trackingId": "HERE-540bb24b-0d57-4f8c-aeaf-6c91cd0aff8d",
  "transportMode": "truck"
}
```

<h1 id="here-tracking-traces">Traces</h1>

The Traces service allows users querying device traces based on time ranges.

A device trace is a device-ingested telemetry along with the ingestion timestamp 
and the device current position.

> **NOTE**:
> Devices should not communicate directly with this service, but should instead send telemetry to
> the ingestion endpoint. Each data ingestion results in an update to the `reported` device shadow 
> and a new device trace creation.

```bash
curl https://example.com/traces/v2/health \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Gets traces within a specified time range

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/traces/v2/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /traces/v2/{trackingId}`

Gets all traces of the device `trackingId` that were recorded within the specified time range. 
The range is defined with `before` and `after` parameters.
The returned traces are sorted in descending order based on their timestamps.

NOTE:
By default, the `after` parameter value is 0, and the `before` parameter is set to the current
system time.
Always make sure to specify `before` and `after` parameters explicitly, as otherwise it may take 
a very long time for the API call to complete.

If the `trackingId` is substituted with a valid `shipmentId`, the response
contains a composition of traces of each shipment segment. 
Traces are only fetched for those segments that are either in `ongoing` or `completed` state.

The `outliers` parameter can be used to select only traces that have
been marked as outliers (if the parameter value is `true`), or only traces
that have not been marked as outliers (if the parameter value is `false`).
If the `outliers` parameter is not present, all the traces will be returned.

The `count` and `pageToken` parameters are used for pagination.


<h3 id="gets-traces-within-a-specified-time-range-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|before|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 1 to the current time.<br>|
|after|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 0 to the current time.<br>|
|outliers|query|boolean|false|Flag specifying if only outliers (`true`) or only nonoutliers (`false`)<br>are to be returned. If the parameter is not present both nonoutlier<br>and outlier traces are returned.<br>|
|mode|query|string|false|Tracker mode.<br>|
|smooth|query|boolean|false|Flag telling if smoothed traces (true) or non-smoothed (false)<br>traces should get returned. By default the traces are not smoothed.<br><br>The smoothing will have an effect on to the stationary trace points only.<br>|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|count|query|integer|false|The number of records per page.|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|mode|unknown|
|mode|normal|
|mode|flight|
|mode|transport|
|mode|sleep|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "data": [
    {
      "payload": {},
      "position": {
        "accuracy": "25",
        "alt": "86",
        "altaccuracy": "96",
        "lat": "52.4988217",
        "lng": "13.35170005"
      },
      "serverTimestamp": 1451425709682,
      "system": {
        "client": {
          "firmware": "10.1.1",
          "hasAttachSensor": true,
          "hasHumiditySensor": true,
          "hasPressureSensor": true,
```

## Deletes all the device traces and events

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/traces/v2/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /traces/v2/{trackingId}`

Deletes all the device `trackingId` traces.

This will also trigger deletion of the entire event history of the device.

|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|

<h1 id="here-tracking-transitions">Transitions</h1>

This service is used to query device transition events.
A transition event is created each time a device enters or exists an associated geofence.

> **IMPORTANT**
> Transitions v2 API is deprecated. Please use Events v3 API instead.


## Gets transitions for a device

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/transitions/v2/devices/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /transitions/v2/devices/{trackingId}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Gets all transitions that were recorded within a specific time range.
Define the range with `before` and `after` parameters.
The returned transitions are listed in descending order based on their timestamps.

Note:
---
By default, the `after` parameter value is 0, and the `before` parameter is set to the current
system time. 
Always make sure to specify `before` and `after` parameters explicitly, as otherwise it may 
take a very long time for an API call to complete.

The `count` and `pageToken` parameters are used for pagination.


<h3 id="gets-transitions-for-a-device-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|trackingId|path|string|true|none|
|appId|query|string|false|Application identifier. Used together with an external ID to identify a virtual device.|
|before|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 1 to the current time.<br>|
|after|query|number|false|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br>The accepted range is from 0 to the current time.<br>|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|count|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "count": 2,
  "data": [
    {
      "geofenceId": "e2f651ee-f196-4fa3-bf88-894dc131dea3",
```

<h1 id="here-tracking-users">Users</h1>

The Users service provides HERE Tracking user authentication and authorization.


## Gets all devices claimed by a project

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/v2/devices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/v2/devices`

Gets all devices claimed by a project.

<h3 id="gets-all-devices-claimed-by-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|projectId|query|string|false|none|
|pageToken|query|string|false|A token from the previously returned response to retrieve the specified page.|
|count|query|integer|false|The number of items to return per page.|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|

|» » » » » » reason|string|true|none|Reason why position was considered to be an outlier.|
|» » » » iccid|string|false|none|SIM card integrated circuit card identifier (ICCID)|
|» » » » imsi|string|false|none|The IMSI of the device's SIM card.<br>|
|» » » » mode|string|false|none|Tracker mode status of the device. When a tracker is in a normal mode, it<br>can send telemetry and, for example, use its GNSS receiver if it has one.<br>A tracker switches into flight mode once it detects that it's in an<br>airplane, and leaves that mode once airplane lands. Transport mode has to<br>be triggered by the user, and it's used, for example, during shipping from<br>continent to another. Sleep mode is used when a tracker is stored in<br>a warehouse, and it's triggered by entering or leaving some defined<br>geofence.<br>|
|» » » » phoneNumber|string|false|none|The phone number of the device's SIM card in the international E.164 format. All the country codes should be prefixed a with "+" instead of "00".<br>|
|» » » » reportedSensorData|object|false|none|The last known device sensor data reported by the device.<br>|
|» » » » » accelerationG|number|false|none|A g-force value of acceleration.|
|» » » » » batteryIsCharging|boolean|false|none|True if device battery is charging.|
|» » » » » batteryLevel|integer|false|none|A value of percentage battery level.|
|» » » » » deviceIsAttached|boolean|false|none|True if device is attached to an object.|
|» » » » » deviceIsStationary|boolean|false|none|True if device hasn't detected movement.|
|» » » » » deviceIsTampered|boolean|false|none|True if device is tampered.|
|» » » » » pressureHpa|number|false|none|A value of pressure in hectopascal.|
|» » » » » relativeHumidity|number|false|none|A value of relative humidity in percent.|
|» » » » » temperatureC|number|false|none|A value of temperature in celcius.|
|» » » » » tiltDegree|number|false|none|A value of tilt in degrees.|
|» » » » stateVersion|integer|false|none|The version of the state of a device. This should be incremented only by HERE Tracking.<br>|
|» » » timestamp|integer|false|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The timestamp of the newest telemetry sent by the device. Note that this is not necessarily<br>the timestamp of all the reported values in the reported shadow since the shadow retains<br>values from previous ingestions if the latest telemetry did not conatain them.<br>|
|» trackingId|string|false|none|This is a unique ID associated with the device data in HERE Tracking. For physical devices the `trackingId` gets assigned to a device when the device is claimed by a user, and for virtual devices it is an external device ID along with the device project `appId`.|

## Gets a user access token

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/v2/login \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "email": "string",
    "password": "string",
    "realm": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /users/v2/login`

Authenticates a user with an email and a password and gets a user access token upon the successful authentication.
The user email must be registered with a valid [HERE Account](https://account.here.com).
Optionally user can provide requested realm ID.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "email": "string",
  "password": "string",
  "realm": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="gets-a-user-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» email|body|string|true|The email address of the user|
|» password|body|string|true|The password of the user|
|» realm|body|string|false|A case-insensitive requested realm ID|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "accessToken": "h1.2...EyS_b6g3uDcKnpknGWQ",
  "expiresIn": 86400,
  "realm": "here",
  "refreshToken": "5qlkthf8mgl5lsrn8br5vdisco",
  "userId": "HERE-12345678-9abc-4def-0123-456789abcdef"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 401,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 401306
  },
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The provided credentials are not valid."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 403,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 403306
  },
  "error": "Forbidden",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The account does not have the correct privileges."
}
```

<h3 id="gets-a-user-access-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success<br><br>The authentication was successful and a valid access token was returned.<br>|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request<br><br>The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range.<br><br>If available, further error details are provided in the response body.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized<br><br>The request did not provide correct authentication details<br>|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden<br><br>The account does not have the correct privileges<br>|Inline|

<h3 id="gets-a-user-access-token-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accessToken|string|false|none|none|
|expiresIn|integer|false|none|The lifetime in seconds of the access token.<br>For example 86400 means the token will expire in 24 hours from the time the response was generated.<br>|
|realm|string|false|none|Current realm ID|
|refreshToken|string|false|none|none|
|tokenType|string|false|none|The token type is bearer|
|userId|string|false|none|The HERE Account ID of a user.|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|integer|true|none|An HTTP status code|
|details|object|false|none|An optional object containing more information about the error|
|error|string|true|none|An HTTP error description|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|An error ID that allows you to trace the error details|
|message|string|false|none|Descriptive text that explains the error|

Status Code **401**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|integer|true|none|An HTTP status code|
|details|object|false|none|An optional object containing more information about the error|
|error|string|true|none|An HTTP error description|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|An error ID that allows you to trace the error details|
|message|string|false|none|Descriptive text that explains the error|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|details|object|false|none|An optional object containing more information about the error|
|error|string|true|none|An HTTP error description|

## Gets a renewed user access token

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /users/v2/refresh`

## Gets a project-scoped user access token

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/v2/tokenExchange \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "accessToken": "h1.2...EyS_b6g3uDcKnpknGWQ",
    "scope": "hrn:here:authorization::myrealm:project/my-project-0000"
  }'
```

`POST /users/v2/tokenExchange`

Takes user access token, requested scope and returns project-scoped user access token.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accessToken": "h1.2...EyS_b6g3uDcKnpknGWQ",
  "scope": "hrn:here:authorization::myrealm:project/my-project-0000"
}
```

<h3 id="gets-a-project-scoped-user-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|X-Request-Id|header|string(uuid)|false|ID used for correlating requests within HERE Tracking. Used for logging and error reporting.<br><br>Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» accessToken|body|string|true|HERE Account user access token, obtained from login endpoint.|
|» scope|body|string|true|Requested scope of the access token. Must be an HRN identifying a project that the identified user has access to.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "accessToken": "h1.2...EyS_b6g3uDcKnpknGWQ",
  "expiresIn": 86400,
  "issuedTokenType": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token",
  "scope": "hrn:here:authorization::myrealm:project/my-project-0000",
  "tokenType": "Bearer"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 400306
  },
  "error": "Bad request",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range."
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 401,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 401306
  },
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The provided credentials are not valid."
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 403,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 403306
  },
  "error": "Forbidden",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The account does not have the correct privileges."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 404,
  "details": {
    "hereErrorCode": 404306
  },
  "error": "Not Found",
  "id": "5771b3d4-95ae-4959-ac63-fbaa3d5d06ee-lds2",
  "message": "The specified resource was not found."
}
```

<h3 id="gets-a-project-scoped-user-access-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success<br><br>The exchange was successful and a valid scoped access token was returned.<br>|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request<br><br>The request object is in an incorrect format or has values that are invalid or out of range.<br><br>If available, further error details are provided in the response body.<br>|Inline|

```json
{
```

```json
  "enabled": true,
  "externalCloudInfo": {
    "extAppId": "ext-app-id",
    "extUserId": "ext-user-id",
    "extUserPassword": "ext-user-password"
  },
  "name": "driver-name",
  "refreshIntervalS": 3600,
  "lastExecTs": "string",
  "totalAddedDevices": 0,
  "createdAt": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|connectorId|string|false|none|Identifier of the connector.|
|projectId|string|false|none|Project ID.<br>Any HERE Tracking user must be a member of a Tracking project.<br>The project ID can be implicitly resolved if the user calling the API is a member of a single project.<br>If the user is a member of multiple projects, the `projectId` query parameter needs to be specified explicitly.<br>|
|description|string|false|none|Brief description of the connector.|
|driverId|string|true|none|Identifier of the driver to be used with this connector.|
|enabled|boolean|true|none|Enabled state of the connector. If set to false then the connector<br>will not execute periodically.<br>|
|externalCloudInfo|object|true|none|An external cloud-specific object that the driver will use to login to the<br>external cloud. The structure of this object varies per driver<br>implementation.<br>It is recommended to have dedicated credentials for logging in to<br>the external cloud in order not to violate possible concurrent users<br>policies of the external cloud.<br>In case of the HERE Tracking loopback driver, the maximum<br>allowed concurrent user account tokens is 3 per account,<br>therefore it is recommended to create a separate HERE account<br>and grant it the required privilege to update the connector's<br>project, and use that account in externalCloudInfo.<br>|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the connector.|
|refreshIntervalS|integer|false|none|This is the interval (in seconds) to execute the sync process<br>between the connector's external cloud and HERE Tracking project.<br>The maximum and at the same time default value for callback-type connectors is 900 seconds.<br>The default value for other type of connectors is 3600 seconds and there is no maximum value set.<br>|
|lastExecTs|string|false|none|Timestamp of the last connection execution.|
|totalAddedDevices|integer|true|none|Number of external devices added to the connector.|
|createdAt|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the connector creation.|

|refreshIntervalS|integer|false|none|This is the interval (in seconds) to execute the sync process<br>between the connector's external cloud and HERE Tracking project.<br>The maximum and at the same time default value for callback-type connectors is 900 seconds.<br>The default value for other type of connectors is 3600 seconds and there is no maximum value set.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_externalCloudInfo">externalCloudInfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaexternalcloudinfo"></a>
<a id="schema_externalCloudInfo"></a>
<a id="tocSexternalcloudinfo"></a>
<a id="tocsexternalcloudinfo"></a>

```json
{}
```

An external cloud-specific object that the driver will use to login to the
external cloud. The structure of this object varies per driver
implementation.
It is recommended to have dedicated credentials for logging in to
the external cloud in order not to violate possible concurrent users
policies of the external cloud.
In case of the HERE Tracking loopback driver, the maximum
allowed concurrent user account tokens is 3 per account,
therefore it is recommended to create a separate HERE account
and grant it the required privilege to update the connector's
project, and use that account in externalCloudInfo.

<h2 id="tocS_registerRequestBodyV3">registerRequestBodyV3</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaregisterrequestbodyv3"></a>
<a id="schema_registerRequestBodyV3"></a>
<a id="tocSregisterrequestbodyv3"></a>
<a id="tocsregisterrequestbodyv3"></a>

```json
{
  "channelType": "webhook",
  "eventSource": "attach",
  "eventType": "BELOW_RANGE",
  "initialState": true,
  "ruleId": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "url": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|channelType|string|true|none|The type of notification channel.|
|eventSource|string|false|none|The event source rule type.<br>|
|eventType|string|false|none|Type of the event.<br><br>An event is created every time an associated rule or geofence is triggered by a device ingestion.<br>The event type depends on the data the device sends.<br><br>Sensors that report numerical data (such as battery, humidity, pressure and temperature sensors),<br>generate an event when the reported sensor reading of the device goes in or out of range, which is configured in the rule.<br>This produces events of BELOW_RANGE, IN_RANGE and ABOVE_RANGE types.<br><br>Sensors that report boolean data (such as attach and tamper sensors), generate events when the device <br>transitions from one state to another, either from `false` to `true` or vice versa.<br>This produces events of FALSE_TO_TRUE and TRUE_TO_FALSE types.<br>The same event types are also generated by the online rule when the device state changes from `offline` <br>(when the device has stopped ingesting data) to `online` (when the device data ingestion has resumed) <br>or vice versa.<br><br>The acceleration sensor generates events whenever the reported sensor reading <br>crosses the acceleration threshold (for example, when the device was dropped).<br>This produces events of the type EVENT. <br>Such events are stateless.<br><br>Events of INSIDE_GEOFENCE and OUTSIDE_GEOFENCE types are generated when the device enters or exits<br>a geofence associated with the device.<br><br>Events of DWELLING_STARTED type are generated when the device has<br>stayed inside an associated geofence for longer than the threshold duration. <br>DWELLING_ENDED type events are generated when dwelling of the device has ended.<br><br>Events of DETENTION_STARTED type are generated when the device has been<br>stationary for longer than the threshold duration, regardless whether the device is inside <br>or outside of any geofence. <br>DETENTION_ENDED type events will be generated when the device starts moving again.<br><br>Events of UNUTILIZED type are generated when the device has been stationary for longer than the<br>threshold duration.<br>UTILIZED type events are generated when the device starts moving again after having been stationary.<br><br>Events of OVERSTOCK, NORMAL_VOLUME and UNDERSTOCK types are generated when the number of assets<br>inside a geofence crosses the `minVolume` and `maxVolume` thresholds of an associated stock rule.<br><br>Events of SHIPMENT_EARLY, SHIPMENT_ON_TIME and SHIPMENT_DELAYED types are generated when a shipment<br>is too early, on time or delayed.<br>|
|initialState|boolean|false|none|Events with the `initialState` property set as `true` are generated when the rule is <br>evaluated for the first time. It indicates the fact that this is the initial evaluation <br>state, which would serve as a starting point for the subsequent rule evaluations.<br>The rest of the rule events would represent a transition of a device or a shipment or <br>a geofence from one state to another and their `initialState` property will be set to `false`.<br>|
|ruleId|string(uuid)|false|none|Must be a valid UUIDv4.<br>|
|url|string|false|none|A webhook URL that will receive notifications POST requests.<br>|

|---|---|

|channelType|email|
|channelType|browserPull|

```json
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the beginning of the interval<br>|
|value|number|true|none|The value of the report metric, which was specified in the `measure` parameter.<br><br>* `measure`: `duration` => `value`: duration of the event in seconds over the time frame<br>* `measure`: `occurrence` => `value`: number of event occurrences during the time frame<br>* `measure`: `day` => `value`: the number of days the event lasted over the time frame<br>* `measure`: `asset` => `value`: the number of assets that generated the event over the time frame<br><br>When `value` is provided along with `timestamp`, the time frame is the specified interval.<br>When `value` is provided with `trackingId` or `geofenceId`, the time frame is the whole report period.<br><br>Additionally, if `method` parameter was given, the `value` represents<br>average/cumulative/percentage of the calculated metric.<br>|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|trackingId|string|true|none|Tracking ID on which the `value` is calculated<br>|
|value|number|true|none|The value of the report metric, which was specified in the `measure` parameter.<br><br>* `measure`: `duration` => `value`: duration of the event in seconds over the time frame<br>* `measure`: `occurrence` => `value`: number of event occurrences during the time frame<br>* `measure`: `day` => `value`: the number of days the event lasted over the time frame<br>* `measure`: `asset` => `value`: the number of assets that generated the event over the time frame<br><br>When `value` is provided along with `timestamp`, the time frame is the specified interval.<br>When `value` is provided with `trackingId` or `geofenceId`, the time frame is the whole report period.<br><br>Additionally, if `method` parameter was given, the `value` represents<br>average/cumulative/percentage of the calculated metric.<br>|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|geofenceId|string(uuid)|true|none|Geofence ID on which the `value` is calculated<br>|
|value|number|true|none|The value of the report metric, which was specified in the `measure` parameter.<br><br>* `measure`: `duration` => `value`: duration of the event in seconds over the time frame<br>* `measure`: `occurrence` => `value`: number of event occurrences during the time frame<br>* `measure`: `day` => `value`: the number of days the event lasted over the time frame<br>* `measure`: `asset` => `value`: the number of assets that generated the event over the time frame<br><br>When `value` is provided along with `timestamp`, the time frame is the specified interval.<br>When `value` is provided with `trackingId` or `geofenceId`, the time frame is the whole report period.<br><br>Additionally, if `method` parameter was given, the `value` represents<br>average/cumulative/percentage of the calculated metric.<br>|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the beginning of the event<br>|
|trackingId|string|true|none|This is a unique ID associated with the device data in HERE Tracking. For physical devices the `trackingId` gets assigned to a device when the device is claimed by a user, and for virtual devices it is an external device ID along with the device project `appId`.|
|value|number|true|none|Duration of the event in seconds|

The response body contains an array of traces, `count` is the number of
returned items and `pageToken` is the next page token if available.

If no traces are found, an object with an empty data array is returned.

Traces are sorted in descending order based on their timestamps.

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|pageToken|string|false|none|A token that can be used to retrieve the next page of the response.|
|data|[object]|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|The desired shadow of the device.<br>|

|system|object|false|none|Contains device configuration settings.<br>|
|timestamp|integer|false|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The time of the last update to the desired shadow.<br>|
|*anyOf*|object|false|none|The `reported` shadow contains the most recent position, sensor readings and settings that the<br>device has sent. The reported shadow may also contain additional properties generated by HERE <br>Tracking based on the device-ingested telemetry.<br>Such properties are stored in `system.computed` property of the shadow.<br><br>In case the most recent telemetry did not contain all the possible<br>fields, the last known information will remain in the shadow. This means that one can<br>see, for example, the last reported temperature or tracker firmware information in the reported shadow,<br>even if the device did not send that information in the latest telemetry.<br>|
|payload|object|false|none|A free format JSON object.<br>The maximum size is 1000B.<br>|
|position|object|false|none|The device location|
|system|object|false|none|Contains device-reported sensor data and device configuration settings.<br>`stateVersion` property contains the version of the last<br>known `desired` state seen by the device.<br>|
|timestamp|integer|false|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.<br><br>The timestamp of the newest telemetry sent by the device. Note that this is not necessarily<br>the timestamp of all the reported values in the reported shadow since the shadow retains<br>values from previous ingestions if the latest telemetry did not conatain them.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_timestampValue">timestampValue</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematimestampvalue"></a>
<a id="schema_timestampValue"></a>
<a id="tocStimestampvalue"></a>
<a id="tocstimestampvalue"></a>

```json
{
  "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "value": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp of the beginning of the interval<br>|
|value|number|true|none|The value of the report metric, which was specified in the `measure` parameter.<br><br>* `measure`: `duration` => `value`: duration of the event in seconds over the time frame<br>* `measure`: `occurrence` => `value`: number of event occurrences during the time frame<br>* `measure`: `day` => `value`: the number of days the event lasted over the time frame<br>* `measure`: `asset` => `value`: the number of assets that generated the event over the time frame<br><br>When `value` is provided along with `timestamp`, the time frame is the specified interval.<br>When `value` is provided with `trackingId` or `geofenceId`, the time frame is the whole report period.<br><br>Additionally, if `method` parameter was given, the `value` represents<br>average/cumulative/percentage of the calculated metric.<br>|

<h2 id="tocS_trackingId">trackingId</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrackingid"></a>
<a id="schema_trackingId"></a>
<a id="tocStrackingid"></a>
<a id="tocstrackingid"></a>

```json
"string"
```

This is a unique ID associated with the device data in HERE Tracking. For physical devices the `trackingId` gets assigned to a device when the device is claimed by a user, and for virtual devices it is an external device ID along with the device project `appId`.

<h2 id="tocS_trackingIdOrShipmentId">trackingIdOrShipmentId</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrackingidorshipmentid"></a>
<a id="schema_trackingIdOrShipmentId"></a>
<a id="tocStrackingidorshipmentid"></a>
<a id="tocstrackingidorshipmentid"></a>

```json
"string"
```

This is a unique ID associated with the device data in HERE Tracking. For physical devices the `trackingId` gets assigned to a device when the device is claimed by a user, and for virtual devices it is an external device ID along with the device project `appId`. Alternatively, a valid `shipmentId` may be used.

### Properties

```json
  "geofenceId": "e2f651ee-f196-4fa3-bf88-894dc131dea3",
  "inOut": "PING_IN_FENCE",

```

| Transition Type          | Meaning                                  |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| PING_OUTSIDE_FENCE       | The device has transitioned outside the geofence. |
| PING_IN_FENCE            | The device has transitioned inside the geofence. |

|---|---|---|---|---|

|timestamp|integer|true|none|Milliseconds elapsed since 1 January 1970 00:00:00 UTC.|
|trackingId|string|true|none|This is a unique ID associated with the device data in HERE Tracking. For physical devices the `trackingId` gets assigned to a device when the device is claimed by a user, and for virtual devices it is an external device ID along with the device project `appId`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|inOut|PING_OUTSIDE_FENCE|
|inOut|PING_IN_FENCE|
|notificationStatus|SENT|
|notificationStatus|NOT_SENT|

<h2 id="tocS_value">value</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavalue"></a>
<a id="schema_value"></a>
<a id="tocSvalue"></a>
<a id="tocsvalue"></a>

```json
0
```

The value of the report metric, which was specified in the `measure` parameter.

* `measure`: `duration` => `value`: duration of the event in seconds over the time frame
* `measure`: `occurrence` => `value`: number of event occurrences during the time frame
* `measure`: `day` => `value`: the number of days the event lasted over the time frame
* `measure`: `asset` => `value`: the number of assets that generated the event over the time frame

When `value` is provided along with `timestamp`, the time frame is the specified interval.
When `value` is provided with `trackingId` or `geofenceId`, the time frame is the whole report period.

Additionally, if `method` parameter was given, the `value` represents
average/cumulative/percentage of the calculated metric.
